docs.text:
usage: cox route [-h]
                 {context,status,file,priority,pull,lint,groups,drift,import,paths,store-fill,approve,decline,edit,remove,requeue,leader,chair,sync,launch} ...

File work for the harness, and see what is queued or running.

positional arguments:
  {context,status,file,priority,pull,lint,groups,drift,import,paths,store-fill,approve,decline,edit,remove,requeue,leader,chair,sync,launch}
    context             the routing profile's resolved context
    status              what is queued or running for this profile
    file                file a new ticket for the harness
    priority            move an initiative up or down the launch order
    pull                file intake tickets from a source, once per link
    lint                static ticket lint over a filed initiative, work-
                        shape.md §3
    groups              print the newest plans/intake-groups/<date>.md file,
                        work-shape.md §5
    drift               items whose store state and file state differ
    import              load the current work item files into the store's
                        work_items table
    paths               rewrite recorded repo paths to the tilde form, dry run
                        first
    store-fill          fill the store's work_items from the workspace files
    approve             approve a draft initiative's todo tickets: todo
                        becomes ready
    decline             decline a draft initiative: its todo tickets become
                        dropped
    edit                change a queued intake, an initiative or a task ticket
    remove              remove a queued intake or an initiative that has no
                        live run
    requeue             requeue the intake of an initiative that has no live
                        tasks
    leader              whether this session is the chair (the SessionStart
                        line)
    chair               the chair lock for the landing loop (runs/chair.json)
    sync                mirror the work store onto the profile's tracker
    launch              run one of the harness's graphs directly

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit

examples:
  cox route launch epic --initiative work/<id> --repo PATH
  cox route status --profile PATH

docs.title: runs
docs.text:
usage: cox runs [-h]
                {usage,trace,clean,land,fetch,review,recover,series,wait,events,top,bar,herdr,notify,detail,stranded,cause,stop,pause,resume,move,triage} ...

What a harness run recorded, and cleaning up after it.

positional arguments:
  {usage,trace,clean,land,fetch,review,recover,series,wait,events,top,bar,herdr,notify,detail,stranded,cause,stop,pause,resume,move,triage}
    usage               usage stats and cost for one run
    trace               the tool-call trace for one run
    clean               delete a run's worktree and branches locally
    land                merge a run's branch into the target repo
    fetch               pull an ended remote lane's run directory, log and
                        branches to this machine
    review              review a contributor PR with the review graph and post
                        the verdict
    recover             merge an approved task's commit into its phase branch
                        after an escalated merge
    series              per-run summary rows across a runs directory
    wait                block until a busy lane's run exits, then print its
                        outcome lines
    events              poll a run's log for structured events
    top                 live table of busy lanes (runs in flight); --once
                        prints it and exits
    bar                 one Waybar JSON line: busy lanes, cost, class
                        idle|running|attention
    herdr               report fleet state (idle|working|blocked) to the herdr
                        pane this runs in; no-op outside herdr
    notify              desktop notifications for exits, quarantines, budget
                        stops and cost
    detail              one run's timeline, objection and last tool calls
    stranded            every approved task record whose work item is not
                        done, with its remedy
    cause               record why one run's attempt at a task was quarantined
    stop                stop a run's process, local or remote, and wait for it
                        to exit
    pause               mark a run paused in the store
    resume              mark a paused run resumed in the store
    move                stop a run at its node boundary and relaunch it on
                        another host
    triage              print a quarantined task's facts; reads the store and
                        git only, makes no model call

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit

examples:
  cox runs fetch <run>
  cox runs land <run> --repo PATH --apply
  cox runs recover <run> <task> --repo PATH
  cox runs usage <run> --json
  cox runs detail <run> --json

usage: cox stats [-h]
                 {ingest,roles,tiers,models,causes,efficiency,gates,explain,series,coverage,bounds,spend-mix,chair,examples,flaky,system-one,lanes} ...

Load the run corpus into the stats store.

positional arguments:
  {ingest,roles,tiers,models,causes,efficiency,gates,explain,series,coverage,bounds,spend-mix,chair,examples,flaky,system-one,lanes}
    ingest              load usage, task, node and launch records into
                        stats.db
    roles               landed rate, attempts-to-land and $/landed per role
                        and model
    tiers               per-role model summaries, a cost-aware pick and the
                        spend it would save
    models              per-role cost, tokens, turns, $/landed and first-try
                        per model id
    causes              quarantined attempts by cause and kind, with sample
                        reasons
    efficiency          cost per turn, cost per landed task, first-try rate,
                        waste share, per day
    gates               what each review, validation and plan gate costs and
                        how often it changes the outcome
    explain             the failure-class breakdown behind one role
    series              per-run summary rows read from the stats store
    coverage            known/total provenance rows for runs, calls and tasks
    bounds              n/p50/p95/max and strict/moderate/liberal candidate
                        ceilings per role and model
    spend-mix           per-model token counts and cost share by class, plus
                        the build-only split
    chair               harness PRs and $, chair $ per PR, hand-finished lands
                        and quarantine $ by cause
    examples            the local system-one backend's training file (JSON
                        lines) from task records
    flaky               tests that needed a serial rerun three times in a
                        week, from task records
    system-one          shadow-to-on graduation report per role, and a
                        proposal for the maintainer to approve
    lanes               per hour, the average and peak busy lanes and the idle
                        minutes, from the store's run spans

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit

examples:
  cox stats ingest
  cox stats ingest runs --db workspace/stats/stats.db
  cox stats roles --json
  cox stats tiers --since 2026-09-01

docs.title: Releases
docs.text: Coxswain is one repository, ppfenning/coxswain, and one package, coxswain. A release is one tag on that repository, one PyPI publish, one GitHub release and one Homebrew formula update.

docs.title: Versions
docs.text:
From 2026.10.0, versions are CalVer: YYYY.M.N, tagged vYYYY.M.N.

  • YYYY is the year and M the month, without a leading zero.
  • N counts the releases cut in that month, from 0.
  • The first monorepo release is 2026.10.0. The next in October would be 2026.10.1. The first in November would be 2026.11.0, not 2026.11.00.

The number says when a release was cut. It does not say whether it is compatible with the one before. Compatibility is carried by the store and workspace schema, which cox setup doctor checks, and by cox setup migrate, which moves a machine across a change in layout.

0.47.0 was the last component release. Releases before it used SemVer-style 0.x numbers across several repositories; they are listed below under Component releases (0.x). See From 0.47 to the monorepo for what changed and how to move.

docs.title: How a release works
docs.text:
A release is cut from the coxswain checkout:

uv run --frozen python -m devtools release <version>

Add --dry-run first to print the plan without running it. --frozen keeps uv run from rewriting uv.lock, since a dirty checkout refuses the cut. --root is where the dash and homebrew-coxswain checkouts sit; it defaults to the checkout's parent.

The cut runs these gates first. Any one refuses it:

  1. The notes page docs/releases/<version>.md exists and has no blank left in it.
  2. Every tree the release tags passes the clean check (.github/check_clean.py).
  3. A release rehearsal passed on the checkout's origin/main commit. --allow-no-rehearsal REASON waives it, and the notes must carry the same reason.
  4. release-check finds no drift between the CLI, the manifest, the docs and the notes. --allow-doc-drift REASON waives it.
  5. Every checkout the release tags is clean, on its default branch, and level with origin/<default>.

Freeze the chair's lands for the cut, so nothing merges under it: cox chair freeze-lands --for 60 --reason "cutting <version>".

Then the steps:

  1. When <version> is above the manifest's version, bump pyproject.toml, uv.lock and manifest.toml on release/<version>, open a pull request, wait for its checks and merge it.
  2. Tag v<version> on the repository. The tag push runs publish.yml, which publishes coxswain to PyPI by trusted publishing. It refuses a tag that is not v plus the CalVer version in pyproject.toml. The release waits for that workflow.
  3. Create the GitHub release coxswain <version> from the notes page.
  4. Open the tap formula pull request, and run the install proof against it (below).

After a cut, or a failed one, the command sends a release_cut or release_failed push to the profile's notify.ntfy topic, when one is set.

Dash lives in its own repository. A release tags it at v<version> only when it has commits since the tag manifest.toml names; otherwise dash keeps its tag. Nothing else is pinned: the checkout is the release.

The docs site is deployed by docs.yml on every push to main, under the manifest's version and latest.

docs.title: The tap pull request and the install proof
docs.text:
Every cut ends with the tap_formula_pr step. It bumps Formula/cox.rb in the ppfenning/homebrew-coxswain tap to the new PyPI sdist on a release branch and opens a pull request there. The tap is what brew install reads, so this pull request is the last gate between a tag and a Homebrew user. --tap-only runs this step alone, for a version already tagged.

Before anyone merges it, the step dispatches .github/workflows/install-proof.yml against that branch as tap_ref and waits for the one run it started. The proof is the clean-machine rehearsal. It runs on two platforms: macOS arm64 on macos-14, and a Linux Homebrew container, homebrew/brew on ubuntu-latest. On each it runs brew install ppfenning/coxswain/cox to install the previous release and checks that the installed version is the one tagged just below the candidate. It stages the candidate formula from the tap branch, then runs brew upgrade cox and fails if the version did not move to the candidate. On a temporary profile, with HOME and the XDG_* directories pointed at a fresh directory, it runs cox --version and cox setup doctor --json and checks both outputs. Then it runs brew uninstall cox and brew install ppfenning/coxswain/cox again, and repeats the same two checks on the clean install.

The release flow never merges the tap pull request. If the proof's conclusion is anything other than success, which is what tap_may_merge tests, the command prints the conclusion and the run URL, leaves the pull request open and exits non-zero. After a pass, you merge the tap pull request by hand.

A proof that cannot fail proves nothing, so .github/workflows/install-proof-negative.yml runs weekly and on dispatch. It feeds the proof the deliberately broken formula tests/devtools/broken_cox.rb. Its own run is green only when the proof failed, so a green run there means the proof failed on that one formula. It does not show the proof catches every broken formula.

A green proof means that formula installs and upgrades on those two platforms today. It does not mean the release is otherwise good.

docs.title: 0.1.0-beta.1
docs.text:
The first Coxswain release, cut on 2026-09-05 — the day the platform took its name. Every component is tagged v0.1.0-beta.1 in lockstep; coxswain and coxswain-tools are published to PyPI by trusted publishing. Status: beta: the loop works and runs itself daily, the interfaces still move. Deprecated for one release: agent-tools as an alias for cox, and cast as an alias for the cartridge's crew key.

Install the platform from one manifest, point it at a repository, describe a change: Coxswain files it, plans it, builds it in a worktree under a budget, has two independent reviewers argue about it, arbitrates them, runs the project's tests as evidence, and hands you a pull request. You merge.

docs.title: coxswain
docs.text: manifest.toml is the single source of truth for what a release installs, with lockstep pins. The docs site: MkDocs Material with mike versions, a CLI reference generated at build time from cox --help, terminal screenshots captured with Rich, every graph's diagram pulled from the graphs repository at build time, and the animated racing-eight header. publish.yml: PyPI trusted publishing on v* tags, no token stored anywhere.

docs.title: coxswain-cartridges
docs.text:
• The coxswain Claude Code plugin: a session-start hook that prints the docket, a statusline, and the /launch, /land, /runs, /intake and /regatta commands.
  • cartridge init <team> writes a minimal team cartridge; cartridge.d/*.yaml fragments fold over each layer, tighten-only, refusals naming the fragment.
  • crew replaces cast as the seats key; policy.dispatch.max_in_flight bounds concurrent runs; policy.plan_tier derives a task's tier from its surfaces; a work item may carry budget_usd.

docs.title: coxswain-graphs
docs.text:
• The coxswain graph's docket reports runs in flight and free slots, and the driver invokes only that many.
  • validate_chunk can ask for evidence by path, which the harness reads once and attaches before asking again — the end of the blind "need to verify" quarantines.
  • A build that hits its ceiling raises BudgetStop with the session and the spend, keeps the partial diff, and the lifecycle decides go/no-go deterministically before continuing in the same session.
  • The plan competition and attack run only where a task's tier reaches plan_competition.min_tier.
  • Every graph's page and diagram are generated from its docstring, with a freshness test.

docs.title: coxswain-tools
docs.text: • cox is the operator command; bare cox opens a Coxswain session. cox install, cox upgrade, cox versions; cox setup doctor and the cox setup screen; cox runs events|top|land; cox route files work, launches the harness detached and reports status; maintainer commands under cox dev.

docs.title: coxswain-crew, coxswain-hud, desktop
docs.text: • coxswain-crew renamed from agent-cast, no behaviour change. coxswain-hud renamed from agent-voice-hud, no feature work. Desktop planned. Both left the product in 0.2.0.

docs.title: Across every repository
docs.text: • Ruff runs in CI with one shared rule set, mirrored by pre-commit.

Cut on 2026-09-17. coxswain-cartridges, coxswain-graphs and coxswain-tools are tagged v0.10.0 in lockstep; coxswain-crew is unchanged and stays pinned at v0.7.0; coxswain-tools is published to PyPI from its tag. Status: beta; nothing here breaks a 0.9.0 install. This release is the fast follow the release tooling itself needed: the planner now gathers component versions at the edge, writes the releases index section, judges the tag-triggered workflow runs, publishes a GitHub Release for every repository it tags, and release-check no longer reports drifts that were never drifts — so this is the first cut made without --allow-doc-drift, and the first to appear on GitHub's Releases pages.

docs.title: coxswain-tools
docs.text:
• The tools release planner gathers each component's pyproject version at the edge and refuses a cut whose manifest and pyprojects disagree (tools #167); its notes check accepts citations of the umbrella repository (tools #170); package_pages judges a README's H1 by the package's own name (tools #168).
  • release-check in tools gains a release_index check that reads the umbrella's releases index in its own table shape, and cox dev release writes that section itself instead of leaving it to the chair (tools #169, #174, #175).
  • wait_workflows in tools waits on the runs the tag itself triggered, not the commit's earlier runs (tools #172).
  • cox dev release in tools publishes a GitHub Release for every repository it tags — the umbrella with the full notes, each component with its own section and a link back — editing an existing release instead of duplicating it; a pinned component gets none (tools #171, #173).
  • cox dev release backfill-github-releases in tools walks the existing tags oldest first and creates the missing Release objects — or edits a stale body, or reports one already current — reading each version's own manifest for a pinned component's tag (tools #179).
  • release-check's cli_surface in tools treats the program name and a group that only holds subcommands as namespaces, ending the seven standing false drifts (tools #177).

docs.title: Known gaps
docs.text: The three graphs-loop-fixes tickets at the attempt cap, the decompose's stale initiative.md on a relaunch, the doctor's schema readers for the other two components and a handful of small loop defects roll forward; the P projects — vendor axis, home/ctop, command table, router and steward, courier — begin next.

docs.title: Components
docs.text: coxswain-tools carries the changes above; coxswain-graphs and coxswain-cartridges are re-tagged in lockstep with no changes of their own. coxswain-crew is unchanged since v0.7.0 and stays pinned there.

Cut on 2026-09-17. coxswain-cartridges, coxswain-graphs and coxswain-tools are tagged v0.11.0 in lockstep; coxswain-crew is unchanged and stays pinned at v0.7.0; coxswain-tools is published to PyPI from its tag. Status: beta; nothing here breaks a 0.10.0 install. This is the release the P projects land in: the vendor axis is real on both sides, the command table has its foundation, the router and the steward exist as commands, and the courier carries a stranded approval from an epic's exit to the chair's inbox — the chair no longer reads run logs to learn what needs landing.

docs.title: coxswain-cartridges
docs.text: • The cartridges providers/local-oss.yaml profile is real: a capabilities block, a per-tier model map with cheap on a local OpenAI-compatible endpoint, and role tiers that never route build, review or arbitrate to the local model (cartridges #78). The umbrella manifest lists local as experimental.

docs.title: coxswain-graphs
docs.text:
• The graphs vendor-axis design fixes the runner contract and the capability declaration a provider profile carries (graphs #128); the runner protocol resolves capabilities per tier and falls up one tier when a role needs one the profile lacks (graphs #129); the Claude Code runner declares its own (graphs #131).
  • The graphs reviewer seats retry a malformed structured output once before the loop counts it (graphs #130); a phase with two unsatisfied parents no longer blocks the epic (graphs #132).
  • The graphs epic sends every approved task it could not land to the chair's courier inbox as a coxswain://task/<id> reference with the land command as its note (graphs #133).
  • The graphs decompose emit keeps only path-shaped entries in a ticket's surfaces and moves anything else to lint (graphs #134); the graphs fix loop's quarantine reason names the verdict that stopped the round, the arbiter's when one ran, not the charter reviewer's (graphs #135); the graphs emit quotes frontmatter scalars that carry a colon, strips a stray closing tag from a body and writes each lint entry once (graphs #136).

docs.title: coxswain-tools
docs.text:
• The tools courier is on: cox courier send, inbox and ack over a committed bus, references resolved by run, finding, PR, proposal, intake, task and initiative (tools #182, #183, #184), by id and not only by path (tools #190), and an entry addressed to the generic chair reaches whichever label holds the leader lock (tools #195).
  • The tools command table has its foundation: the design (tools #186), a byte-for-byte --help snapshot of the runs group taken before the change (tools #187), and the runs group built from agent_tools/commands.py with the snapshot proving the output identical (tools #188).
  • The tools router and steward exist: the design contract (tools #189); the pure select_tier with a floor, a minimum sample size and a deterministic one-in-N challenger schedule (tools #191); the challenger column populated at ingest and reported apart from standard calls (tools #192); cox router select with the off|shadow|on flag read from the routing profile (tools #193); the steward's evidence bar and proposal rendering for the ceiling case (tools #194); and cox steward propose, which writes candidates as intake files and never edits a profile (tools #196).
  • cox home in tools gains its health panel (tools #181); the decompose refreshes a stale initiative.md from its intake on relaunch (tools #185); the GitHub Releases backfill skips a component with no checkout and says "would create" or "would edit" in a dry run (tools #180); the live GitHub Release step names the previous release's tag in an "unchanged since" body, never the tag it is creating (tools #197).

docs.title: Known gaps
docs.text: The router runs in off by default and nothing in the graphs harness calls cox router select yet; the steward emits ceiling proposals only. The remaining command groups migrate to the table one ticket each, with their snapshots taken first. The task record still lacks its initiative and phase, so an escalated approval's printed remedy is recover where land is the one that works; that, the clean guard for a refused task's draft branch, and the from-intake filer's slugs and surfaces roll forward.

docs.title: Components
docs.text: coxswain-cartridges carries the local provider profile; coxswain-graphs carries the vendor-axis runner contract, the courier send and four loop fixes; coxswain-tools carries the courier, the command table foundation, the router and the steward. coxswain-crew is unchanged since v0.7.0 and stays pinned there.

Cut on 2026-09-17. coxswain-cartridges, coxswain-graphs, coxswain-tools and coxswain-crew are tagged v0.12.0 in lockstep, the crew rejoining the release version with its first change since v0.7.0; coxswain-tools is published to PyPI from its tag. Status: beta; nothing here breaks a 0.11.0 install. This release saves a long day's work before the weekly budget closes: the command table now builds the whole CLI, the release planner performs its own bumps, the weekly spend ceiling is real, and the operator surfaces that had been waiting since the sixth land — the in-place drill-down in cox runs top, the Waybar line, the home screen's paint and regatta.

docs.title: coxswain-crew
docs.text: • The crew gains Liam, the courier seat: it reads the courier inbox for the chair's label, resolves each reference through the CLI, relays it to its owner in the harness's own words, and acks only what it delivered; cheap tier, read-only tools, no write authority beyond the ack (crew #6).

docs.title: coxswain-graphs
docs.text:
• The graphs epic writes initiative and phase into every task record and prints cox runs land as the remedy for an escalated approval, since recover could not resolve a phase without them (graphs #138).
  • The graphs fix loop's lint-fix step lands (graphs #139).

docs.title: coxswain-tools
docs.text:
• The tools command table now builds every command group — courier, home, versions, usage, plan, epic, stats, setup, route and dev — from module-level rows in COMMAND_TABLE, each proven byte-identical by the help snapshot taken before its migration (tools #199, #200, #201, #203, #204, #207, #208, #211, #219, #226, #227).
  • cox dev release in tools lets a planned bump through the gate and executes the bump, push, PR, wait and merge steps itself, so a cut needs no hand-made version PRs (tools #217, restored by #222).
  • The tools routing profile gains spend.weekly_ceiling_usd with a 93 percent hard stop judged by launch, context and home alike (tools #210, #211), and the weekly total reads the cost and start time a usage file actually carries (tools #221, #222).
  • cox runs top in tools expands a run in place under its own row on ENTER, collapses on ESC, and keeps the expansion while j and k move (tools #214, #215); cox runs bar prints one Waybar line with the launcher on click (tools #216).
  • cox home in tools gains its framed layout, the paint pass and the regatta view (tools #212, #218, #224); the window pane shows percent of ceiling (tools #220); the stats regime history is backfilled (tools #223).
  • cox route file --from-intake in tools writes word-boundary slugs, surfaces from the body's paths and a full ticket frontmatter (tools #205); cox runs clean keeps a refused task's draft branch (tools #206); the doctor's schema row reads the other two components' versions from their checkouts (tools #202); the notes citation check no longer reads a coxswain:// reference as an umbrella mention (tools #209); launching or landing takes the leader lock when nobody holds it (tools #213).

docs.title: Known gaps
docs.text: The render and surface-check steps of the command table are still ahead, as are the home screen's regatta lane and layout, three operator-surface tickets, and the intake sources, recover record and route sync initiatives; all are filed and fenced. cox runs clean keeps the per-task phase branch of a refused task where it should keep the agents draft. The umbrella's own release check now runs clean.

docs.title: Components
docs.text: coxswain-tools carries nearly all of the changes above; coxswain-graphs carries the task-record fields and the lint-fix step; coxswain-crew carries the courier seat and rejoins lockstep at v0.12.0; coxswain-cartridges is re-tagged in lockstep with no changes of its own.

Cut on 2026-09-17. A patch: coxswain-cartridges, coxswain-graphs and coxswain-tools are tagged v0.12.1 in lockstep; coxswain-crew is unchanged and stays pinned at v0.12.0; coxswain-tools is published to PyPI from its tag. Status: beta; nothing here breaks a 0.12.0 install. This release fixes a fresh-machine install that had been broken since the repositories were renamed on 2026-09-05: the installer looked for checkouts under names that no longer exist.

docs.title: coxswain-cartridges
docs.text: • The plugin marketplace declares itself coxswain-cartridges, the repository's name since the rename; until now every Claude Code install registered the marketplace and the local-skills plugin as agent-cartridges (cartridges #81).

docs.title: coxswain-tools
docs.text: • cox setup install, the setup and cartridge screens and the CLI's default provider profile and skills root build their paths from the coxswain-* checkout names. Under the old names a fresh install failed at its first step, uv venv in a directory that does not exist, and an existing install only worked because its profile had been repointed by hand. The marketplace the installer registers is now local-skills@coxswain-cartridges (tools #229).

docs.title: Known gaps
docs.text: The cartridges Python distribution is still named agent-cartridges: the graphs shell extra and the graphs CI checkout depend on that name, so the rename is a graphs-and-cartridges pair still ahead. The routing profile stays at ~/.config/agent-tools/profile.yaml and the agent-tools command alias stays for this release, as planned. An install made before this release keeps its old marketplace registration until local-skills@agent-cartridges and the agent-cartridges marketplace are removed and cox setup install --plugins is rerun.

docs.title: Components
docs.text: coxswain-tools and coxswain-cartridges carry the changes above; coxswain-graphs is re-tagged in lockstep with no changes of its own; coxswain-crew is unchanged and stays pinned at v0.12.0.

Cut on 2026-09-24. coxswain-cartridges, coxswain-graphs and coxswain-tools are tagged v0.13.0 in lockstep; coxswain-crew is unchanged and stays pinned at v0.12.0; coxswain-tools is published to PyPI from its tag. Status: beta; nothing here breaks a 0.12.1 install. Every graph call used to name its model tier in code. It now names a role and optional hints, and the tier comes from the provider profile's per-role defaults. Those defaults were set to the tiers the call sites used before, so no role's tier changes in this release. The cartridges side of the model router lands complete. The work store gains a one-way mirror onto a GitHub Projects board, the landing loop gains gate levels, and the operator surfaces planned since 0.12.0 are finished.

docs.title: coxswain-cartridges
docs.text:
• The cartridges model router lands as pure parts: the chair's bounds as one typed record (cartridges #83), the budget rule (cartridges #84), the model catalog and its loader (cartridges #85), the tier rules (cartridges #86), and core.router.decide, which composes them into a model, effort and budget triple clipped to the chair's bounds and names each bound that clipped it (cartridges #87). The pacing states it accepts are the ones the tools pacing check actually returns: go, go_degraded and stop.
  • Every provider profile's defaults: block names a tier for every role the graphs call, each at the tier its call site named before, so the graphs change below leaves every role where it was (cartridges #124).

docs.title: coxswain-graphs
docs.text:
• The graphs runners record a CallDecision for every call: the requested and chosen tier, the model, the reason, and for Claude Code the CLI version from the stream's init event (graphs #145, #146, #147).
  • The graphs tier resolver picks a call's tier from overrides, then the tier the caller named, then the profile's per-role default, then the floor, and both runners resolve through it (graphs #148, #149, #150). Graphs never import the cartridges router: a runner records a model, effort and budget it is given, and never computes or clips one.
  • The graphs call sites in ops triage, phase validation, initiative decompose and the lifecycle graph name a role and hints instead of a literal tier (graphs #267, #268, #269, #270). Decompose's adversary keeps its literal deep, so it stays a tier above the lifecycle adversary.
  • The graphs build step can no longer write outside its scratch checkout into the phase branch (graphs #142), may run python -m pytest and python -m ruff (graphs #144), and a check that fails after approval goes back into the fix loop instead of ending the task (graphs #143).
  • A ticket may list verify: commands, and the graphs harness runs them itself, so a reviewer no longer asks the builder for output it is not allowed to produce. They run in the build's own scratch checkout after the patch; handoff and both reviewers see their output, marked as harness-run, and so do validation and the phase check. A failing verify command is evidence, never a quarantine (graphs #151, #271).
  • The graphs CallDecision gains six optional system-one fields, backend, mode, answer, confidence, threshold and agreement, for the Jev deciders' shadow mode; old rows load with them unset (graphs #273).

docs.title: coxswain-tools
docs.text:
• cox route sync in tools mirrors the work store onto a GitHub Projects board, one way: an issue per item in the item's own repository, a State, Phase, Run, Cost and Gate field per board item, and the issue number written back to the item. It plans every step with a pure function, prints the plan under --dry-run, and refuses an item whose state has no column or whose repository no longer resolves (tools #240, #244, #432). Every land now syncs the one item it touched, and its pull request closes that item's issue (tools #434).
  • The tools landing loop gains gate levels, ticket, phase, epic and full, read from runs/policy.gate.json, defaulting to ticket and tightening only. A land the gate stops short of its merge prints where it stopped and which pull request it left open, and exits 3 (tools #239).
  • cox install --edge in tools installs every component from its branch tip instead of its tag (tools #241), and cox dev release opens the Homebrew tap's formula bump from the sdist PyPI lists (tools #242).
  • cox runs recover in tools resolves a real task record, reading the phase from the record's path and the initiative from the work store (tools #235). cox runs clean keeps the right branch for a refused task (tools #234).
  • cox home in tools gains the regatta lane and a panel layout that can be reordered, hidden and resized from the keyboard and is remembered between sessions (tools #237, #238).
  • The release planner in tools updates the component tags in the manifest's inline tables (tools #231), waits when GitHub has not yet scheduled a pull request's checks instead of failing (tools #232), and checks how the notes cite a version already cut (tools #233). The home screen's slow-reader test no longer depends on wall-clock time (tools #236).
  • cox dev commands render in tools writes the README's Commands section from the command table, and reproduces the committed text byte for byte (tools #435).

docs.title: Known gaps
docs.text: The cartridges work store drops a ticket's verify: list when it reads the ticket, so the graphs verify step above has nothing to run yet; the fix is first in 0.13.1. The graphs model router's shadow mode and CLI version pin are held until they are rescoped around the rule that graphs never import the cartridges router. The epic driver runs a task whose state is blocked, and cannot follow a dependency into another initiative. cox runs land refuses a stacked task after its parent lands, and does not resume when its pull-request branch already exists. All are filed. The Jev system-one deciders, the intake sources and the rest of the command-table migration are ahead.

docs.title: Components
docs.text: coxswain-graphs and coxswain-tools carry most of the changes above; coxswain-cartridges carries the router and the provider defaults; coxswain-crew is unchanged and stays pinned at v0.12.0.

Cut on 2026-09-24. coxswain-cartridges, coxswain-graphs and coxswain-tools are tagged v0.14.0 in lockstep; coxswain-crew is unchanged and stays pinned at v0.12.0; coxswain-tools is published to PyPI from its tag. Status: beta; nothing here breaks a 0.13.0 install. The Jev system-one deciders land complete and off by default, with a vendor backend and a fully local one. Model selection moves to capability classes without changing a single role's model. A ticket can now ask for a stronger model, and a build sent back for changes escalates on its own. The landing loop resumes where it stopped, lands stacked tasks, and reads every board card and check at a fraction of the GitHub API calls it used.

docs.title: coxswain-cartridges
docs.text:
• The cartridges work store keeps a ticket's verify: list (cartridges #128) and its per-role tier: map (cartridges #134) instead of dropping fields it did not know, and a ticket may depend on a task in another initiative, met once that task is done (cartridges #130).
  • The cartridges router speaks capability classes (extract, reason, judge, frontier): the chair's bounds hold a class ceiling (cartridges #141), decide enforces it (cartridges #143), and a router Decision has a plain JSON wire form a caller can hand to graphs, which never imports cartridges (cartridges #144).
  • Every provider profile maps classes to models (cartridges #142). Its per-role defaults stay tier names for this release: writing them as classes (#146) was reverted (#147) because the graphs runner still checked tier names only; that check is being fixed.
  • The route-work skill uses the cox route chair commands and names the two launch gotchas (cartridges #132).

docs.title: coxswain-graphs
docs.text:
• Jev system-one deciders land complete and switched off unless a provider profile's system_one block turns them on: the arbiter is skipped when both reviewers approve (graphs #277); the typed fast-path core (graphs #278) and its wiring into the build runner (graphs #285); a handoff spec, a shadow report and a review prescreen (graphs #279, #280, #282); a backend over TypeSafe's Jev API (graphs #281); and a local k-nearest-neighbour backend that needs no vendor (graphs #298). A decider that fails never fails a node.
  • Elevation. A ticket's tier: map raises a role's model and never lowers a call site's own, and a build sent back after a review revise asks one tier higher on its second attempt and records why (graphs #283).
  • Capability classes. The resolver and both runners choose models through classes, falling back to tiers when a profile has no class map (graphs #299, #300, #301), and the runner can record a router decision it is given without computing one (graphs #302).
  • The driver honours dependencies on tasks in other initiatives (graphs #284), and the coverage floor no longer passes when pytest collects nothing (graphs #275).

docs.title: coxswain-tools
docs.text:
• cox runs land resumes on a pull-request branch it already pushed when the tree matches (tools #443), lands a task stacked on a parent that already merged, and finds a phase's initiative from the work store (tools #445). It reads an arbitration record that is null, a dict or the arbiter-skip marker (tools #437).
  • cox route sync updates one card with one issue read instead of listing the whole board, and every land polls its checks over the REST API, off the GraphQL budget that evening rate limits kept exhausting (tools #447). A ticket gets its issue when it is filed, a pull request closes it, and a done ticket's issue is closed (tools #459).
  • A run counts as live only if its process started after the run was launched, so a pid reused after a reboot no longer holds a slot (tools #441). The ready list skips work behind a blocked item, and cox route launch refuses it unless --include-blocked is given; --force never lifts that guard (tools #444).
  • Pacing does not judge the spend-to-time ratio before 10 percent of a window has passed, and the launch line says "advisory" instead of claiming a downgrade it does not apply (tools #446). cox reads capability-class names in profile defaults (tools #461).
  • The release planner bumps a component whose manifest entry spans several lines (tools #439).

docs.title: Known gaps
docs.text: Profile defaults written as classes return once the graphs runner accepts class names. The graphs capability-classes shadow phase and the route-sync card fields (per-task Run and Cost, initiatives as parent issues) are in flight for the next release. The cox dev commands move to the umbrella's unshipped devtools/ after this cut; 0.15.0 is the first release cut from there. SQLite run records are decomposed and their first phase is building.

docs.title: Components
docs.text: coxswain-graphs carries Jev, elevation and the class-aware runners; coxswain-cartridges carries the class vocabulary, the router wire form and the work-store fields; coxswain-tools carries the landing, sync and pacing fixes; coxswain-crew is unchanged and stays pinned at v0.12.0.

Cut on 2026-09-25. coxswain-cartridges, coxswain-graphs and coxswain-tools are tagged v0.15.0 in lockstep; coxswain-crew is unchanged and stays pinned at v0.12.0; coxswain-tools is published to PyPI from its tag. Status: beta; nothing here breaks a 0.14.0 install. This is the first release cut by the umbrella's own devtools, now that the release commands have left the published cox CLI (coxswain #76). The release index keeps the manifest's order and is committed with the manifest bump, so a cut no longer leaves the umbrella dirty (coxswain #82). The devtools messages and the README marker name devtools (coxswain #83, #84). System one defaults to shadow with the local backend: it answers beside the handoff node, never instead of it, records every answer next to the node's own, and turns itself off quietly on a machine that cannot run it. A report says when a role has earned on, as a proposal for the maintainer. Run records gain a SQLite store that graphs owns, written alongside the files the tools still read. The chair's own cost and the harness's are now measured side by side.

docs.title: coxswain-cartridges
docs.text:
• Provider profiles write their per-role defaults as capability classes, with every role on the same model as before (cartridges #149); the graphs runners and cox read class names since graphs #309 and tools #461.
  • System one defaults to shadow with the local backend in the Claude Code and local profiles: a kNN decider over the handoff role at threshold 0.9, reading ~/.local/state/coxswain/system_one/handoff.jsonl (cartridges #152). Shadow answers beside the node and never replaces it. Nothing leaves the machine. The hosted-API profile carries no block.
  • The release-sync skill names the umbrella's devtools release commands (cartridges #151).

docs.title: coxswain-graphs
docs.text:
• System one records and degrades. Every call's usage row carries its decision, with the fast path's backend, mode, answer, confidence, threshold and whether it agreed with the node (graphs #329). A backend that cannot serve (a missing key, a missing or empty examples file, an optional package not installed) turns system one off for the run with one system-one: off (<reason>) line instead of failing it; a malformed block still fails (graphs #332). The local backend expands ~ in its examples path (graphs #334).
  • Capability classes, shadow phase. The runner protocol accepts a router decision through a DecisionSource (graphs #312); both runners record a supplied decision beside their own and never compute one (graphs #305, #306); the lifecycle, phase-validation, decompose and triage call sites pass one on every call (graphs #324, #325). The Claude Code runner enforces a profile's CLI version pin or floor and records a violation (graphs #313). The runners accept class names wherever they accepted tiers (graphs #309).
  • A single graph run can write its result as JSON for its caller with --result-out (graphs #343).
  • A state_move proposal names approved, never done. The work-state arm writes what the proposal names, so every approved task used to read done before cox runs land merged it (graphs #344).
  • SQLite run records. Graphs owns the schema. One connection URL selects SQLite or Postgres with portable placeholders (graphs #308); numbered migrations apply on open (graphs #311); migration 0001 holds the run-record tables, ledger, gate decisions and lease (graphs #317) and 0002 the graph registry (graphs #319); trace events go to per-run day files compressed with zstandard (graphs #315); a leader lease carries a monotonic fencing epoch (graphs #321); a loaded graph registers its definition and content hash once (graphs #327); and idempotent writers cover every run-record table (graphs #331). Given a store, the runners record every call and its decision (graphs #336), and the epic driver records phases, tasks, attempts, gate decisions and ledger rows, fencing each leader-only write with the lease epoch (graphs #338). Every graph run now opens the store at start: the profile's storage_url, or cox.db in the runs directory. It registers the graph and writes the run row, and a run whose record cannot be kept does not start (graphs #340). One connection serves the runner's thread pool, with a lock that keeps another thread's statement out of an open transaction (graphs #341). The record files are still written exactly as before; the store is written beside them. A read module answers run summaries, cost by model, calls, attempts, ledger rows, gate decisions, the current lease and a run's graph (graphs #346). Two backfills import the existing record files and loose traces. Each reports row counts and archives its sources only when asked and only when the counts balance; neither deletes anything (graphs #348, #350). docs/STORAGE.md in graphs covers the tables, the lease and its fencing epoch, the read path, the Postgres step and the chair's backfill runbook (graphs #352).

docs.title: coxswain-tools
docs.text:
• Chair measures. cox runs land appends every land to runs/land.jsonl with the steps it reached (tools #470); chair.json records the chair's Claude session, and the chair's cost is priced from its transcripts (tools #471); a quarantined attempt carries a cause, and cox runs cause and the quarantine spend split by cause (tools #474); cox stats chair reports harness PRs and spend, chair spend per PR, hand-finished lands and quarantine spend by cause (tools #476).
  • cox route sync puts the run and each task's cost on its card and makes an initiative the parent issue of its tasks (tools #464).
  • cox dev is gone from the published CLI; it prints where the release tooling moved and exits 2 (tools #442).
  • cox stats examples --role handoff|review_charter writes the local system-one backend's examples file from the task records, with the same state text the system-one layer builds at run time (tools #477).
  • cox stats system-one reports, per role, the shadow rows since the last model or Claude Code version change, their coverage, agreement and the costly-direction disagreements, and a READY or NOT YET verdict against 100 rows, 95% agreement and at most 1% costly. --propose writes a graduation proposal for the maintainer, with the calls it would save and the risk it takes, and never edits a profile (tools #479).
  • cox route pull [--source github] [--dry-run] files an intake ticket for each new item a source lists, once per link. It refuses a repository the profile's repo_map does not map, and marks the source item with the intake path. The profile gains sources and repo_map (tools #481). A pull also sends each open pull request labelled review to cox runs review, then relabels it review:taken so the next pull skips it (tools #488).
  • cox runs review --pr <url> runs the review graph on a contributor's pull request, in a fresh worktree of the local checkout the profile's repo_map names, and posts the verdict as a review with inline comments. It refuses a repository with no checks interpreter, as cox runs land does, and never merges (tools #486).
  • The README Commands block lists the new commands (tools #480, #487).
  • The tools repository pins Python 3.12, the CI version, so the byte-exact help fixtures are written the way CI reads them (tools #478).

docs.title: Known gaps
docs.text: The SQLite cutover, where graphs stops writing the record files, waits until the tools read the store and the backfill counts are verified on a real workspace. Until then the files remain the record the tools read. The graph registry stays empty in practice: no graph declares a loaded graph object yet, so a run row's graph id is unset. Shadow runs only where the graphs system-one-local extra (sentence-transformers) is installed and cox stats examples has written the examples file. Without either, it stays off and prints its one-line reason. Only the handoff role has a default; the review prescreen needs its own examples file. The Jira and Asana intake adapters are built but held, because the tools repository names no vendor.

docs.title: Components
docs.text: coxswain-graphs carries the run-record store, system one's recording and degrade path, and the capability-class shadow phase. coxswain-tools carries the chair measures, the system-one examples and graduation report, cox route pull and cox runs review. coxswain-cartridges carries the shadow default and the class-named defaults. coxswain-crew is unchanged and stays pinned at v0.12.0.

Cut on 2026-09-25. coxswain-cartridges, coxswain-graphs and coxswain-tools are tagged v0.16.0; coxswain-crew is unchanged and stays pinned at v0.12.0; coxswain-tools is published to PyPI from its tag. Status: beta. Git is now the only requirement for landing work: cox runs land goes through a pluggable forge, local by default (plain git) and GitHub built in. The tools read their run records through one layer that prefers the record files and falls back to the SQLite store, and the backfill imports a real workspace with nothing left unreadable. That readies the cutover planned for 0.17.0. System one shadows a second role, the review prescreen. From this release the umbrella's devtools tag only the components that changed since their last tag (coxswain #90, #91). Its README render understands nested commands (coxswain #93), the tap step leaves the tap clone on its branch (coxswain #87), and the install page tells you to trust the tap first, as current Homebrew requires (coxswain #88).

Upgrading from 0.15.0. Two defaults change. Landing uses the local forge and cox route sync mirrors nothing, unless the profile says otherwise. To keep landing through GitHub pull requests and syncing a GitHub Project as before, add forge: github and tracker: github-projects to ~/.config/agent-tools/profile.yaml.

docs.title: coxswain-cartridges
docs.text:
• The review prescreen joins handoff in the local shadow default, and both read one examples file, ~/.local/state/coxswain/system_one/examples.jsonl (cartridges #157).
  • The local cartridge's lint check carries its safe fix, ruff check --fix ., so the harness fixes what ruff can before it calls a task approved (cartridges #154). Ruff is pinned to the version CI runs (cartridges #155).

docs.title: coxswain-graphs
docs.text:
• A yes/no system-one question reads only the yes/no examples, so one examples file serves every role (graphs #362).
  • The stored phase record carries its manifest's content, the proposals included (graphs #357).
  • The records backfill imports a workspace as it really is: runs paired with their launch records, epic runs that wrote only phase manifests, calls from before call ids (under a stable legacy: id), launch-only runs, and attempts from before attempt kinds. Files that are not records are skipped, and every run that has a usage file is stamped as ended. The first full import of this workspace reads zero malformed records, and archiving refuses while any remain (graphs #355, #360, #364, #365). Ruff is pinned to the CI version (graphs #358).

docs.title: coxswain-tools
docs.text:
• Forges. cox runs land finds, opens, checks and merges through the forge the profile names, with forge: local (plain git) the default and forge: github built in. Other forges register by entry point under coxswain.forges (tools #518, #520, #524).
  • Trackers. cox route sync mirrors the work store through the tracker the profile names: tracker: none (the default) mirrors nothing, and tracker: github-projects is built in. A run can still pause sync with runs/policy.tracker.json, which wins over the profile (tools #551).
  • cox setup doctor checks for git, and for gh only when the forge is github, and a fresh machine gets one next step instead of a column of failures. cox versions names cox install when there is no manifest (tools #526).
  • Read layer. run_store answers a run's usage, calls, phase manifests and trace events, reading the record files first and an ended run in the SQLite store after them (tools #492, #494, #496, #509, #513). The usage readers, cox runs series, cox runs trace, the phase land, notifications, the usage window, route sync's costs, the stats commands and cox stats ingest all read through it (tools #498, #500, #502, #504, #532, #540, #549).
  • Intake adapters that name a vendor live outside tools and register by entry point under coxswain.sources; Jira and Asana moved to the new ppfenning/coxswain-sources (tools #506).
  • cox route status shows live and recent runs, and --all shows every run (tools #530).
  • The ccusage active block is cached for a minute in the runs directory, so pacing checks seconds apart run it once (tools #544).
  • route chair, route launch and route sync join the command table as nested commands, so go/commands.json, the README and the Go port all see them (tools #542).
  • The profile's forge and tracker keys are documented, with the right default profile path (tools #545, #552).
  • cox stats system-one restarts its graduation window only on a model change (tools #505), and cox stats examples writes several roles into one file (tools #522).
  • cox runs land lands a task stacked on a parent that merged as a squash (tools #533), and marks done a landed task whose run also recorded a quarantine (tools #535).
  • pytest --regen rewrites the help and command-table snapshots, and CI checks the README Commands block against the umbrella's renderer (tools #511, #490). Ruff is pinned to the CI version (tools #516).
  • Go spike (not shipped). go/ holds a Go port of the CLI. The command table exports to go/commands.json (tools #507, #510). The Go help renderer matches 51 of the 52 help fixtures byte for byte (tools #515, #547), and usage assess gives the same answer as Python on this workspace (tools #528, #536, #538). Help renders in 2 ms against 72 ms and in 11 MB against 23 MB.

docs.title: Known gaps
docs.text: The SQLite cutover is next (0.17.0). Graphs still writes the record files, and the store is written beside them. Live views read a per-call trace spool, which the cutover keeps and compacts when each call ends. Trackers registered under coxswain.trackers resolve, but route sync runs only the built-in GitHub Projects sync for now. GitLab, Bitbucket and Gitea forges are not written yet.

docs.title: Components
docs.text: coxswain-tools carries the forges, the trackers, the read layer, the doctor and the Go spike. coxswain-graphs carries the backfill and the manifest in the store. coxswain-cartridges carries the second shadow role and the lint fix. coxswain-crew is unchanged and stays pinned at v0.12.0.

Cut on 2026-09-25. coxswain-cartridges, coxswain-graphs and coxswain-tools are tagged v0.17.0. coxswain-crew is unchanged and stays pinned at v0.12.0. coxswain-tools is published to PyPI from its tag. Status: beta. This release carries two headlines.

Run records live in the store alone. A run writes no usage file, no per-phase manifest file and no per-call file. Its totals, phases, gate decisions, ledger rows and calls are rows in the run store (runs/cox.db). Each call's stream events are compacted into runs/traces when the run ends. The task records under runs/<run>/tasks/ stay files, because landing and resuming read them.

A vendor-neutral core, with liveness from the store. Every integration that names a vendor is a plugin in the public ppfenning/coxswain-plugins, found by entry point: intake sources, system-one backends and runners, as forges and trackers already were. A run holds a lease in the store and renews it with a heartbeat, so "is this lane alive" no longer depends on a process id. One live run per epic is enforced by that lease, and a stale run's writes are fenced.

This workspace ran on the store alone from 8:01 AM ET on the day of the cut: 59 runs and 763 model calls, with nothing written outside the store but task records and logs. Parallel runs are called lanes now, in the regatta vocabulary. The umbrella's release-check no longer files a bullet under the umbrella for naming coxswain.forges or coxswain-sources, and keeps a dotted path inside its sentence (coxswain #96). The docs gain a Plugins page (coxswain #97) and a Dashboards page (coxswain #103).

Upgrading from 0.16.0. Nothing to change in the profile. zstandard is now installed with coxswain-tools. System one is off unless a provider profile configures a backend. Install coxswain-plugins in place of the archived coxswain-sources for the Jira and Asana intake sources. Record files from earlier runs are still read first. python -m harness.store_backfill imports them into the store, and archiving them is optional. The store migrates itself to schema version 3 on the next run; the migration adds a nullable runs.host. The new extras are optional: postgres to read a Postgres store, parquet for Parquet traces, and lake for the Iceberg lake.

docs.title: coxswain-cartridges
docs.text:
• core.manifest.append_ledger writes a manifest's ledger rows without writing the manifest file, and record_run is the file write plus append_ledger (cartridges #160).
  • The provider profiles no longer turn system one on. The local kNN backend could not reach the graduation bar, and it is removed (cartridges #161).

docs.title: coxswain-graphs
docs.text:
• Store-only run records. The CLI prints a run's totals from the store and writes no usage file (graphs #372). The epic driver writes no per-phase manifest file and requires a store (graphs #374, #375). The runner writes no per-call file, and the CLI compacts the run's trace files into the trace store at run end (graphs #377). A single-graph run records to the store like a one-phase run (graphs #393).
  • Leases. Every run holds the store lease runs:<prefix> and renews it every 30 seconds from a heartbeat thread. A transient store error is retried (graphs #399). A second run of the same epic is refused while the lease is held, and the epic driver's writes are fenced by the lease's epoch (graphs #386). A run stopped with SIGTERM still records its end and releases its lease (graphs #370).
  • Plugins. Runners are found by name, with claude-code and anthropic built in; an unknown runner refuses instead of falling through to another (graphs #384). System-one backends are found by entry point, and the kNN and Jev built-ins are gone (graphs #382). A hosted backend reads its key only from system_one.key_env, never from the provider's own key (graphs #378).
  • An OpenAI-compatible runner for local models: a chat client, schema-shaped answers from plain text, and the runner (graphs #395, #397, #403). It is built in as runner: openai-compatible, and a hybrid profile hands its anthropic/ models to the Anthropic runner on the same run (graphs #414, #416).
  • Each call records a runner-neutral summary (tool uses, reads, result) in the store (graphs #380).
  • The store's tests run against a real Postgres in CI (graphs #405). A built-in model-tier system-one backend and an offline evaluator exist but are not turned on (graphs #388, #391).
  • An epic run branches from the repository's default branch, not from whatever the checkout has out (graphs #368).
  • A lint fix is amended into the task's commit, so a task branch stays one commit and lands without a hand squash (graphs #412).
  • python -m harness.store_copy copies a SQLite store into Postgres, idempotently (graphs #407).
  • The decompose ticket lint treats a URL route as notation and flags a ticket that names another repository's file (graphs #389, #401).

docs.title: coxswain-tools
docs.text:
• Reads for the store alone. A killed run's usage, a live run's phases, and a finished run's calls and last tools all come from the store (tools #563, #565, #576). cox runs trace uses each call's stored summary (tools #586).
  • Liveness from the lease. Route status, the launch guard, runs top and the docket decide a run is live from its store lease, with the pid as a fallback for older runs (tools #588). One read of the leases table serves a whole docket (tools #610). The docket shows each busy lane's heartbeat age, and the regatta and runs top flag a lane whose heartbeat has stopped (tools #593, #598).
  • Lanes. cox says lanes where it said runs in flight (tools #584). cox runs wait blocks until a busy lane finishes and prints its outcome. cox stats lanes reports busy and idle lanes by hour (tools #602, #604, #605).
  • cox runs land never moves the checkout. The pull-request branch is built and checked in its own worktree, which links the repository's .venv (tools #570, #572).
  • A launch never reuses a run number whose files are gone (tools #581).
  • cox runs land fast-forwards a local default branch that is behind its remote before it builds the pull request, and refuses one that has diverged (tools #632).
  • cox setup doctor lists the plugins each side can load (tools #591).
  • The run store can be read by URL, SQLite or Postgres, with the postgres extra (tools #596, #600, #609, #622). The README says what each command reads from a shared store (tools #613).
  • cox setup doctor has a store row: the store's kind and run count, or why it did not answer, never the URL (tools #624). It also says whether Parquet traces are readable (tools #630).
  • CI runs the lake, Parquet and Postgres tests in an extras job with a Postgres 16 service (tools #623).
  • zstandard is a base dependency, because a run's traces live only in the trace store (tools #578). The Go port is removed: Coxswain stays with Python (tools #579).
  • Usage assessment reads each run record once, only inside the last seven days (tools #574).
  • The route lint treats a URL route as notation and flags a ticket that names another repository's file (tools #594, #607). cox route sync's help names the profile's tracker (tools #561).

docs.title: Groundwork for 0.18.0 (in the tags, not yet wired)
docs.text:
• Parquet traces: the column mapping, the pyarrow extra, the traces-root resolver, and reading and writing a run's Parquet file with the zstd day files as fallback, in graphs (graphs #409, #411, #418, #420). Compaction does not write Parquet yet. tools reads a run's Parquet trace file before the zstd day files (tools #615, #617, #628). tools reads them from the profile's traces_url, once per run (tools #646).
  • The Iceberg lake: the lake extra (pyiceberg with a SQL catalog, duckdb), table definitions, and a sync that appends each ended run's rows once behind a per-table mark (tools #619, #621, #626). Also trace registration in place with add_files, read-only DuckDB queries over the lake tables, and lake doctor checks (tools #634, #636, #638). No cox lake command yet.
  • Superset: a compose deploy under deploy/superset with DuckDB and read-only access to the runs directory (coxswain #99, #104). A Coxswain dashboard as code, installed by a one-shot service once Superset is healthy (coxswain #101), and a Dashboards docs page (coxswain #103).
  • Lanes on several machines: runs gain a nullable host column (graphs #422, migration 0003), and tools reads the lanes a shared store says are live. The docket and runs top can render a remote lane, but the commands do not list them yet (tools #640, #642, #644).

docs.title: Known gaps
docs.text: Lanes on several machines are the headline of 0.18.0. The chair stays on the machine that runs cox and keeps the workspace; other machines run lanes against a shared Postgres store. The pieces above are in the tags, but nothing launches a lane on another machine yet. Graphs does not yet compact traces to Parquet, and cox lake has no commands yet. Superset charts do not save a query context, so the chart data API cannot run them. The dashboard itself builds its queries in the browser. System one is parked: neither the local kNN nor a cheap model reached the graduation bar offline.

docs.title: Components
docs.text: coxswain-graphs carries the cutover, the leases, the plugin lookups, the OpenAI-compatible runner and the store copy. coxswain-tools carries the store-only reads, liveness from the lease, the lane commands, the store URL and the lake modules. coxswain-cartridges carries append_ledger and the profiles without system one. The umbrella carries the Superset deploy and dashboards. coxswain-crew is unchanged and stays pinned at v0.12.0.

Cut on 2026-09-26. coxswain-cartridges, coxswain-graphs and coxswain-tools are tagged v0.18.0. coxswain-crew is unchanged and stays pinned at v0.12.0. coxswain-tools is published to PyPI from its tag. Status: beta. This release carries three headlines.

Lanes on several machines. The chair is the machine that runs cox. It keeps the workspace and does all landing, and other machines run lanes against a shared Postgres store. cox setup doctor --host <name> checks a lane machine over ssh. cox route launch epic --on <name> allocates the run on the chair, copies the initiative over and starts the lane there. The docket, cox route status and cox runs top show the lane with its host and heartbeat, and the store's lease refuses a second run of the same epic on any machine. When the lane ends, cox runs fetch brings its task records, log and branches home, and cox runs land lands them as usual. Verified end to end with a Docker container as the lane machine. The docs page Several machines covers the setup (coxswain #120, #133).

A data platform. Every run's traces are written as one Parquet file per run, zstd inside, and the old traces are converted: in the reference workspace, 1.12 GB of JSONL became 269 MB across 712 runs. cox lake sync appends each ended run's records to an Iceberg lake, cox lake query runs DuckDB over it, and a land syncs the lake when a catalog exists. The Superset dashboard reads the SQLite store or a shared Postgres store. In Postgres mode each DuckDB connection attaches the store from COXSWAIN_STORE_URL in the container, so no URL or password is saved in Superset (coxswain #114, #116, #118, #131, #136). deploy/superset/check.py plans both modes offline and confirms every chart returns rows (coxswain #108, #134).

A harness that learns from its own records. A quarantined attempt records its cause: the ticket, the code, the review or the harness. A rule decides first, then a cheap model. cox stats causes, cox stats gates, cox stats tiers and cox stats efficiency report where attempts fail, what each review step costs and changes, the cheapest model per role that keeps its landed rate, and the cost per landed task. The dashboard gains an Efficiency section, a quarantines-by-cause chart and review verdict charts (coxswain #110, #122, #126), and a Lake and Efficiency docs page (coxswain #124). On the reference workspace, builds land 98% of the time on Sonnet at $1.23 per landed task, against 92% on Opus at $2.14. On 2026-09-25, 199 tasks landed at $3.71 each, 63% on the first build.

The umbrella's release-check exempts every line of a deprecation sentence and keeps a wrapped citation on its bullet (coxswain #112, #129), and the releases page lists the newest release first (coxswain #127).

Upgrading from 0.17.0. The store migrates itself to schema version 6 on the next run: task_records (0004), attempts.cause and cause_why (0005) and work_items (0006). The record files stay authoritative this release. A team cartridge may set apply_arm: workstore on state_move, item_create and item_update, so the harness makes those ticket writes in code instead of with a model call. CI's required test job runs Python 3.14, and a py312 job keeps the floor. To use Postgres, install coxswain-tools[postgres] and set storage_url in the provider profile on every machine.

docs.title: coxswain-cartridges
docs.text:
• workstore is a valid apply_arm without being a role, beside shell and pr (cartridges #165).
  • CI runs the suite on Python 3.14 (cartridges #163), and the required test job now runs it, with a py312 floor job (cartridges #167).

docs.title: coxswain-graphs
docs.text:
• The CLI stamps the run's host at run start, and the store copy carries it (graphs #425, #427, #433).
  • Trace compaction writes one Parquet file per run under the profile's traces_url. It deletes the loose files only when the new rows are all there, and leaves them in place on any failure (graphs #429, #461). python -m harness.store_backfill_traces repacks historic traces into Parquet and archives the sources (graphs #431, #434).
  • python -m harness.store_traces dump <root> <run_id> prints a run's Parquet rows as JSON lines, for readers without pyarrow (graphs #436).
  • Calls recorded before calls had ids carry one id everywhere. The store names them legacy:<run>:<seq>, and python -m harness.store_backfill_traces relink rewrites the Parquet traces to match (graphs #445).
  • Every per-ticket node call records its task id, so review steps join to their tasks (graphs #443).
  • Task records are mirrored into the store: migration 0004, the upsert, read, write, copy, the driver's mirror and a backfill (graphs #439, #441, #447, #449, #451, #465, #467).
  • A quarantined attempt records its cause: migration 0005, a deterministic rule, then a cheap classifier, written to the store and backfilled (graphs #453, #455, #469, #473, #476, #478). A budget, turn or limit stop is harness (graphs #479), and so is the older plural check-failure message's code (graphs #493). python -m harness.store_classify gives historic unknowns the classifier's cause, bounded and recorded as a run (graphs #495).
  • A good build whose answer mentions the usage limit is no longer read as the account's limit banner. A quarantine reason is capped at its first line (graphs #485).
  • python -m harness.store_cli is the one writer other tools use: mark-landed, set-state and the chair's lease. It requires --store-url or --runs-dir, so it never creates a stray store (graphs #457, #459, #471, #475, #499).
  • Work items in the store: migration 0006, the mirror rule, store read and write, the driver's mirror and a backfill (graphs #481, #482, #489, #491, #501).
  • The workstore arm carries out a state_move, item_create or item_update proposal in code, and falls back to the model arm when the proposal lacks its fields (graphs #484, #487).
  • A relaunch recreates a phase branch whose tasks are already done, instead of refusing (graphs #463).
  • Reviewers are told which commands the builder's session could run, and never ask for evidence from any other (graphs #505).
  • The required test job runs Python 3.14 and CI runs the suite on it, with a py312 floor job (graphs #437, #497).

docs.text:

  • cox route status and the docket list lanes that other machines hold in the shared store, with their host (tools #656).
  • A cox without pyarrow, such as the Homebrew install, reads Parquet traces through the harness's own Python (tools #666).
  • Lanes on another machine: lane_hosts in the routing profile, the ssh, rsync and git argv builders, the remote-lane record, and cox setup doctor --host (tools #660, #662, #664, #670).
  • cox route launch --on and cox runs fetch (and --all) (tools #673, #684, #686, #688, #694, #720). The launch records the repository, so cox runs fetch brings an epic lane's branches home (tools #749). A lane launched on another machine never takes that machine's chair lock (tools #751). cox setup doctor reads a new, empty store as ok, with "no runs yet" (tools #753).
  • cox runs land records no PR for the local forge (tools #755). Its note for a merged item that was still ready names both reasons: quarantined after approval, or run on another machine (tools #757).
  • cox stats gates reads review verdicts from the store, and flags a step only with at least 50 decided tasks (tools #668, #671, #677, #728, #730). cox stats tiers (tools #679, #690). cox stats causes (tools #702). cox stats efficiency and the docket's efficiency line (tools #716, #724, #726).
  • cox runs land reads a task's record from the store first, falling back to the file (tools #692, #696). It regenerates the README's Commands block before it commits (tools #700, #713, #714).
  • Writes to the store go through the harness's store CLI: the land's mark-done and the chair's lease (tools #698, #706, #708, #711, #722).
  • Work state through the store: the set-state wrapper, the work-items reader, the land's and the route's state mirror, and cox route drift (tools #732, #734, #737, #739, #741).
  • cox route sync drives a tracker plugin through sync(workspace, items, *, dry_run) (tools #743).
  • The store's JSON columns read the same from Postgres as from SQLite (tools #747).

docs.title: Known gaps
docs.text: The chair holds the workspace, so a lane's task records come home by cox runs fetch, and only the chair lands. Moving task state and records into the store, so any machine could land, is next. Each target repository must sit at the same absolute path on a lane machine. Traces stay on the machine that ran the lane unless traces_url names shared storage. The Efficiency charts' landing history starts when runs/land.jsonl began.

docs.title: Components
docs.text: coxswain-graphs carries Parquet traces, the cause of a quarantine, task records and work items in the store, the store CLI and the workstore arm. coxswain-tools carries the lake commands, lanes on another machine, the stats commands, the store-first land and the tracker plugin contract. coxswain-cartridges accepts the workstore arm. The umbrella carries the Superset Postgres mode, the Efficiency charts and the docs. coxswain-crew is unchanged and stays pinned at v0.12.0.

Cut on 2026-09-26. coxswain-graphs and coxswain-tools are tagged v0.19.0. coxswain-cartridges is unchanged and stays at v0.18.0, and coxswain-crew stays pinned at v0.12.0. coxswain-tools is published to PyPI from its tag. Status: beta. This release carries two headlines.

Any machine can land (opt-in). Set work_state: store in the provider profile on every machine, and the shared store becomes the source of truth for task state. The harness reads a task's state from the store, where the row wins over its ticket file. It writes a state move to the store first, as a compare-and-set, then repairs the file. cox runs land on any machine checks that the task is approved in the store and holds a land:<task> lease around the merge. It marks the task done with a compare-and-set, so a second machine's land of the same task stops before it merges. The ticket files become a cache that python -m harness.store_cli regenerate-states rebuilds. cox runs fetch brings only branches when the store already holds the lane's records. The default stays work_state: files, and nothing changes without the key. Verified end to end with a Docker container as the lane machine: it landed its own lane, and the chair's land of the same task stopped with "another machine landed it". The Several machines docs page explains the setup (coxswain #142).

Storage beyond one machine, local-first. Traces and the Iceberg lake reach a self-hosted S3-compatible server, such as Garage, through an object_store block in the provider profile. The block holds the endpoint, the region, the names of the environment variables with the key and secret, and path-style addressing. Credentials come only from the environment. Any other URL scheme comes from a plugin in the new coxswain.storage entry-point group, so core names no cloud vendor. The docs cover a plain shared path first, then object storage (coxswain #140).

Upgrading from 0.18.0. Nothing to change. work_state and object_store are optional. Recorded costs are now each call's own spend: a resumed call used to record the session's running total. python -m harness.store_backfill --recost-resumed corrects the history (the reference workspace's recorded harness spend fell by $502, about 15%).

docs.title: coxswain-graphs
docs.text:
• Work state in the store: the work_state key, the authority rules, compare-and-set set_state, store_cli set-state --expect (exit 3 on a mismatch), the driver reading the store, store-first state moves, and store_cli regenerate-states (graphs #510, #512, #518, #522, #524, #530).
  • s3:// traces use the provider profile's object_store block (graphs #514). Other schemes resolve through the coxswain.storage entry-point group (graphs #520).
  • A resumed call records its own cost, and store_backfill --recost-resumed corrects recorded history (graphs #516, #526).
  • The handoff sees the commands the builder's session could run, and discharges a demand for any other command instead of sending the build back (graphs #508, #528). Builds may also run uv run pytest, uv run ruff and git -C on their own scratch checkout (graphs #534).
  • Scope no longer proposes item_create for a ticket that is already a work item, so no model call is spent on a write that changes nothing (graphs #532).
  • Phase validation runs only once a phase is finished. A partial phase records goal_met: false without a model call (graphs #538).
  • Every handoff and review round is kept in the task record's fix_loop.rounds (graphs #540).
  • Under work_state: store, a store-first move writes the ticket's state line in code, so the file and the store agree (graphs #536).

The version string drops the -beta.1 suffix: under zero-dot versioning the major already says the interface may move and the minor is where breaking changes go. docs.title: coxswain
docs.text: The HUD and desktop leave the product: four components, not six; cox install --with hud|desktop and cox hud are gone, and the voice loop lives on in its own repository (#25, #26). The methodology states what a graph may not do: a graph owns sequence and writes nothing, one harness owns every consequence (#24); the front page, tagline, licence and animated header (#16–#21); the README is the package's long description (#22); post-rename repository names and resolving docs links (#23).   • cox dev release-check — CLI surface, manifest and release-notes citation checks; cox dev release refuses to tag while a drift stands unless --allow-doc-drift says why (tools #53, #59, #61).
