Cut on 2026-09-26. coxswain-cartridges, coxswain-graphs and coxswain-tools are tagged v0.20.0. coxswain-crew stays pinned at v0.12.0. coxswain-tools is published to PyPI from its tag. Status: beta. This release carries two headlines.

The chair runs itself. cox chair run is the chair's mechanical loop. Each tick (default 60 seconds) it beats the chair lease, reads the 5-hour window and the weekly spend, lands every approved task one repository at a time, relaunches an initiative once its ready tasks' dependencies have landed, retries or rescues a quarantine caused by the harness, fills free lanes up to the team cartridge's policy.dispatch.max_in_flight from the work store first, and prints one status line.

Past the weekly hard stop it lands, but launches nothing. Every action it takes carries the lease epoch, so when an interactive session takes the chair with cox route chair take --steal, the loop stops acting until the chair is released. cox chair run --once --dry-run plans one tick and changes nothing. It never cuts a release, merges a Homebrew tap PR, pushes the workspace, or changes a profile or tier. The Autonomous chair docs page describes it (coxswain #146).

Rescue. A build quarantined for a harness reason that kept its patch no longer needs a person to finish it. The graphs rescue graph re-applies the patch in a fresh worktree, runs the configured checks in the harness itself, and runs the review round. On approve, the task lands as usual. A rescue runs at most once per version of the ticket, and a failed rescue does not count as a build attempt. cox route launch rescue runs it, and cox chair run plans it in place of a rebuild.

Upgrading from 0.19.0. Nothing to change. The chair loop is opt-in: start cox chair run when you want it. Attempts now record the ticket text they were made against, so after a ticket is rewritten the attempt cap counts only attempts on the new text.

docs.title: Components
docs.text: coxswain-tools carries the chair loop and the rescue action. coxswain-graphs carries the rescue graph and the attempt cap. coxswain-cartridges carries the ticket-version stamp. The umbrella carries the docs. coxswain-crew is unchanged.

Cut on 2026-09-27. coxswain-cartridges, coxswain-graphs and coxswain-tools are tagged v0.21.0. coxswain-crew stays pinned at v0.12.0. coxswain-tools is published to PyPI from its tag. Status: beta. This release carries two headlines.

The chair runs a fleet. cox chair run fills the local lanes first, then each lane_hosts entry up to the same cap, launching a remote lane with cox route launch epic --on <host>, and it fetches a remote lane's records and branches before it lands the lane's approved task. A host whose Claude login has lapsed is refused before any lane starts, and cox setup doctor --host says so. The loop's weekly spend comes from the store's node_calls, so a loop on one machine sees the whole account's spend. Every action the loop performs is recorded in the store's chair_actions table as well as the JSONL file, so any machine on the shared store can see what the loop did. cox chair service --install writes the user unit that keeps the loop running on a resident machine. A human takeover carries an expiry (cox route chair take --hours, extend), and the loop takes the chair back when it passes. The store gains a hosts table for the fleet's machines, written by store_cli host upsert|beat|set-state, and cox host add|list|drain|activate|beat|doctor|sync manage it; the planner reads capacity from the table when it has rows.

Drafts. A draft is an initiative whose tasks are todo and whose initiative.md says draft: true and who proposed it. cox steward draft turns the steward's grounded proposals into drafts and lists the ones it cannot ground. cox route approve <initiative> moves a draft's tasks to ready; cox route decline drops them with a reason. The loop never launches a draft; its status line counts them (drafts N) and cox route status lists them with proposer and age. todo is held everywhere now: ready plus a needs edge is the only gate, and the graphs driver fixtures say so.

Upgrading from 0.20.0. Nothing to change on one machine. For a fleet: put the S3 key names and the AWS SDK checksum settings in one env file sourced by the login shell on every machine (the Several machines page has the lines), run cox host add for each lane host once the table exists, and run cox host sync after a graphs release lands so no host is behind the store's schema version. Two new migrations (chair_actions, hosts) apply on the first open.

docs.title: coxswain-cartridges
docs.text: • ready_tasks returns only tasks in state ready whose needs are done; todo, blocked, approved and in_progress are held (cartridges #173).

Status: beta. This release makes the chair loop steady on its own, and it carries three headlines.

The loop lands what it can and waits for what it must. A phase counts as complete when every task in it is done, approved or dropped, so a phase with several approved tasks lands instead of waiting on itself. The loop relaunches an initiative only after its last run has an exit record, removes the previous run's phase worktrees before a relaunch, and treats a branch clear that finds nothing as done. Dropped work and missing repositories are skipped in the stranded listing. The loop's own lands and launches never claim the chair lease, and a land into a repository another land holds refuses instead of racing it.

Fewer hand merges. Tickets in one phase that share a file are merged into one ticket before lint and launch. When two tasks' changes only add lines at the same spot, the land keeps both sides and lets its checks decide.

Spend counted by the meter's own week. spend.weekly_reset (for example "Sun 04:00 America/New_York") anchors the weekly window at the meter's reset instead of a rolling seven days. The loop, the launch gate, route context and usage assess all count the same week, and the status line shows where the week began.

Upgrading from 0.21.0. Nothing to change on one machine. To count the week the way the meter does, add weekly_reset under spend: in the profile. A fleet can give each lane host its own capacity with cox host add <name> --ssh <dest> --capacity <n>; the local cap stays the team cartridge's policy.dispatch.max_in_flight, and it applies per machine.

Status: beta. This release lets the fleet run itself, and it carries four headlines.

The store is the board. Work items live in the store (graphs harness.store_queue, migration 0009), intake states agree between the ticket files and the store, and cox route drift compares intake rows as well as tasks. A machine whose profile names a shared Postgres storage_url now reads its board from the store when the store answers, and says work state: files (store unreachable) when it does not; a local SQLite store keeps the ticket files, so local-first stays the default.

A lane host can come and go. A lane whose host has gone quiet and whose own lease heartbeat has stopped is marked lost and relaunched elsewhere; hosts can be drained, and placement weighs hosts and their capabilities. The loop checks each lane host's Claude login every 30 minutes over ssh, records it with the host's beat, and gives a host with a lapsed login no new lanes. A remote run's approvals reach the chair's ticket files when it is fetched, and so do its phase branches.

The chair is resident and has a console. cox chair service --install --host <name> prints or runs the steps that put the chair loop on a lane host as a user service, and --status --host reports it. cox console is one terminal screen of drafts, hosts, lanes, the chair and needs-chair items, whose keys run cox commands after a y/n. Stale work becomes a draft for a person to approve or decline.

One merge to main per phase. The loop lands a completed phase as one squash of its branch onto a fresh main, from its own pr/ branch, and marks every task in it done; a partial phase's branch is carried forward on relaunch with main merged into it, and an approved task of a partial phase waits for its phase instead of landing alone.

Upgrading from 0.22.0. Run the graphs migration (0009) against the store. A lane host needs the tools' postgres extra. To make a machine a resident chair, run cox chair service --install --host <name>, then the two steps it prints for a person (loginctl enable-linger and systemctl --user enable --now).

This patch settles the decisions the operator made the morning after 0.23.0, and it carries two headlines.

A build checks its cost at every guide and stops at a $6 failsafe. A build runs in slices. Each slice stops at the guide, the build's measured shape (about $1.90 today), where the harness judges go or no-go: the session can resume, the partial work stays inside the task's surfaces, and each slice changed something. A build that passes resumes, as many times as it takes, until its session's cumulative spend reaches the $6 failsafe; then it is refused with a split recommendation. The weekly cap stays the global bound.

Run logs keep a 7-day lookback. cox lake sync archives each ended run's text log and call log older than log_retention_days (default 7) beside the traces on the object store, reads each copy back, and only then removes the local file. The loop's trace prune keeps the same number of days.

Two decisions need no code. The resident chair never pushes the workspace: the store is the board. Postgres stays the setup default: the shared provider profile names the fleet's store, and a machine falls back to SQLite only when no store is named.

Upgrading from 0.23.0. Nothing to change. To keep logs longer, set log_retention_days in the routing profile, after every machine runs 0.23.1, since an older cox refuses a key it does not know. A provider profile that keeps its own copy of the Claude Code profile adds role_ceiling_usd: {build: 6.0} beside role_budget_usd.

Status: beta. This release makes builds watch their cost, gives the console the fleet's picture, teaches the loop to get itself unstuck, and moves the dashboards onto the store and the lake. It carries four headlines.

Builds watch their cost, and the failsafe caps the whole build. A build's checkpoints now weigh richer go/no-go signals, with their positions taken from the measured bounds and every decision written to a ledger. The $6 runaway ceiling from 0.23.1 capped each call rather than the session, so a build that resumed could spend it again on every call; it now caps the session's cumulative spend and refuses a call once the ceiling is spent. The per-task budget estimator lands here too, and is wired into launches in 0.24.1.

The console shows the fleet. cox console shows each lane's run with its stage and cost, each machine with its lanes in use against capacity (the local machine included), the chair's liveness, and the 5-hour and weekly spend, with every time in the viewer's local timezone. cox runs top names each run's machine in a column of its own.

The loop gets itself unstuck. A re-grounded ticket is retried after harness failures, counting attempts on its current body only. An approved task waiting for the rest of its phase no longer holds back its siblings' relaunch. A phase land finds each task's record in the run that approved it and takes the run's own initiative, so a phase name shared across initiatives lands. A remote launch brings the lane host's checkout up to date before the lane builds, and in store mode a fetched remote run's approvals come from the store. A runaway-ceiling stop reaches the chair as its own runaway cause, and the ticket lint refuses a needs edge inside one phase.

The dashboards read the store and the lake. The Fleet and Chair datasets read the store's real columns, the probes ask with WHERE false, the history datasets read the Iceberg lake on the object store through the store's catalog, and landed tasks come from the store's task records, so the Superset deploy runs on any machine that reaches the store and the object store, with no runs directory.

Upgrading from 0.23.1. Restart the chair loop after upgrading cox: a running loop keeps the planner it started with. To share the lake's catalog across machines, set lake_catalog_url in the provider profile to the store's Postgres URL. A Superset deploy adds COXSWAIN_S3_ENDPOINT (host and port, no scheme), COXSWAIN_S3_KEY_ID, COXSWAIN_S3_SECRET and COXSWAIN_S3_REGION to its .env, drops COXSWAIN_RUNS_DIR, and needs the object store reachable from its containers; run the dashboards bootstrap twice on a new server, since the store and lake are probed once the database exists. Ten of the twenty-five charts still name dataset columns that changed, and are fixed in 0.24.1.

Status: beta. This release paces the fleet from the plan meter, fills every machine's lanes, and teaches the loop to guard its own lands; it also lays the backend for coxtop, the terminal dashboard coming in 0.26. It carries four headlines.

Builds pace themselves. The chair loop and the launch gate read the Claude plan meter the status line records, label every figure meter or est, and calibrate the fallback ceilings over the meter's own window, so a stale reading no longer turns into a false usage stop. Every build task gets its own budget from the p75 cost of similar landed tasks, clamped to $1 to $4; the per-thread stop at 1.5 times that budget was reverted in this release because a build that hit it could wedge its run, and returns once that wait is fixed.

Lanes on any machine. Relaunches and retries go to any machine with a free lane, not only this one, while an initiative's runs stay on its home machine until that machine drains, loses its login or loses its lane. Each machine's lane capacity is set at run time with cox host capacity, cox runs move moves a run to another machine, and the loop treats its own machine as local rather than as a remote lane host.

The loop guards itself. After every tools or graphs land the loop runs a smoke check (cox route context, cox runs top, a dry-run tick); on a failure it holds launches, flags the land and opens a revert PR for it. A lane with no node call for 30 minutes is flagged as stalled, and the epic driver dumps every thread's stack on SIGUSR1. Lands got safer: a phase land merges main in first when its parent phase already landed, keys earlier runs' records correctly, reads task states and records from the store in store mode, and refuses when an approved task's files are missing from the squash; a fetched remote run counts as fetched, and an initiative decomposed into no tasks is flagged.

coxtop's backend. cox dash --feed streams a versioned JSON snapshot of the fleet and cox dash --detail serves drill-downs for a run, an initiative, a machine, spend, health and release. cox runs stop acts on a run on any machine. cox runs pause and resume are in the CLI but fail in this release (see Known issues); the driver's pause wait between nodes is in, but nothing can set a pause yet. The decompose can number tasks by ordinal (t1, t2, ...) so no model writes a full task id.

Upgrading from 0.24.0. Upgrade every machine that reaches the shared store together: this release migrates the store to schema version 10, and older code refuses a newer store. Restart the chair loop after upgrading cox; a running loop keeps the planner it started with. The dashboards' charts now all match their datasets; rerun the dashboards bootstrap after upgrading.

Status: beta. This patch fixes a 0.25.0 regression that broke every runner except Claude Code, and it stops the build checkpoint from sending back good builds. It carries two headlines.

Every runner works again. 0.25.0 passed the pause hook to every style pass and gate model-arm apply, but only the Claude Code runner accepted it, so the Anthropic runner (the default when a profile names no runner), the OpenAI-compatible runner and System One failed there with a TypeError. Every runner now takes the hook and waits before its request when the run is paused, and a test checks that every runner accepts every keyword of the runner protocol.

The build checkpoint judges scope on the change, not its tests. A checkpoint sent a build back as soon as its partial work touched a file outside the task's surfaces, and on 2026-09-29 it did so 37 times, 13 of them for nothing but tests, fixtures or snapshots. Tests, test fixtures and .snap files now count as inside a task's surfaces, a surface ending in / covers the files under it, and untracked scratch files a build drops (probes, diffs, outputs) are ignored. Review still judges all of them.

Upgrading from 0.25.0. Nothing to change: no store migration. Restart the chair loop after upgrading cox.

Cut on 2026-09-30. coxswain-graphs, coxswain-tools and coxswain-dash are tagged v0.26.0. coxswain-cartridges stays pinned at v0.23.1 and coxswain-crew at v0.12.0. coxswain-tools is published to PyPI from its tag. Status: beta. This release brings coxtop, the fleet dashboard, as a preview. It carries three headlines.

coxtop, a preview. coxswain-dash joins the release as an optional component. It provides coxtop, a terminal dashboard for the fleet built with ratatui. It shows the chair, spend, machines, lanes, runs, the queue and the inbox on the Regatta and Slipstream pages, with a Harbor Light toggle. You can drill into a run, an initiative or a machine. It reads cox dash --feed and cox dash --detail, and every action it offers is a cox command it shows you before it runs. coxtop is a beta and is actively being improved. The visuals will move toward the design canvas in 0.27, and a panel to talk with the chair is planned. Install it with cargo (the crate is coxswain-dash; it installs coxtop):

cargo install --git https://github.com/ppfenning/coxswain-dash --tag v0.26.0

Short ids from the store. Intakes and initiatives get short ids from a sequence in the store (store migration 0011). Existing work gets short_id aliases backfilled. Commands accept either the short id or the full slug and show the id next to the title.

Store migrations back up first. Before a pending migration, the store writes a backup: pg_dump -Fc for Postgres, the backup API for SQLite. python -m harness.store_migrate --pending <url> lists what would run without applying it.

Upgrading from 0.25.1. The store migrates to schema 11 the first time the new code opens it, after writing a backup to $COX_STORE_BACKUP_DIR (default ~/.local/state/coxswain/backups/). Postgres needs pg_dump on the path, or set COX_STORE_MIGRATE_WITHOUT_BACKUP=1 to migrate without one. Upgrade every machine that shares a store together, because older code refuses a newer schema. Restart the chair loop after upgrading cox.

Status: beta. This release opens intake to work beyond Coxswain itself: any project, with or without a GitHub remote. It carries three headlines. The coxtop work planned for 0.27 (the chair panel, cox chair ask, the canvas visuals, API runner cost recording) moves to 0.28.

Intake from a drop folder. A new built-in source, folder. Each Markdown file dropped directly in a configured folder becomes an intake ticket, titled by its first # heading or its file name, and moves into the folder's done/ once filed. repo_map maps each folder to the repository its tickets target. cox route pull with no --source now pulls every source the profile names, in order, so the autonomous chair reads the folder alongside GitHub issues.

sources: {"github": {"repos": ["owner/repo"]}, "folder": {"repos": ["~/intake"]}}
repo_map: {"owner/repo": "/path/to/repo", "~/intake": "/path/to/repo"}

Projects with no GitHub remote. A new built-in forge, auto, picks per repository from its origin: one on github.com lands through pull requests and their checks, any other, including one with no remote at all, through plain git with the land's own checks as the gate. One profile can now hold both kinds of project.

GitHub intake works with current gh. gh 2.102 removed the repository field from gh issue list --json, which made every GitHub pull fail before it listed anything. The source now reads the repository from each issue's URL.

Upgrading from 0.26.0. Nothing migrates. A bare cox route pull used to read github; it now reads every source in the profile and says no sources in the profile when there are none, so pass --source github to keep pulling one source. Set forge: auto to land projects off GitHub. Restart the chair loop after upgrading cox.

Status: beta. This release lets the chair run on any machine, moves lands off the chair's tick, and brings the chair into coxtop. It carries four headlines.

The chair runs on any machine. The run-liveness check and the SIGTERM that stops a run's children now work on macOS, which has no /proc. A remote run's progress shows in the feed, and a phase branch is carried to the host where the relaunch runs. A lane host's readiness check follows the runner, and a lane host with no plan meter of its own uses the one the chair publishes. The chair's status line now lives in the store, so the feed reads it from any machine.

Lands no longer hold up launches. Lands run on a land worker, so a tick launches work while a long land runs, and the chair keeps beating its lease during the land. A repo-lease refusal now counts as busy, and a stopped chair releases the leases its land worker held.

Talk with the chair from coxtop. cox chair ask, cox chair answer and cox chair decisions let the chair put a decision to you and take your answer. coxtop gains a chair panel that hosts the chair's session, and a chair card that shows the current action, the last tick, today's counts and the age of the last beat.

API runners record cost and honor the budget. Every API runner records cost and tokens and stops at budget_usd. They build through a vendor-neutral tool-calling loop with an Anthropic adapter, get their own working directory, and a model arm refuses a runner that cannot use tools.

Upgrading from 0.27.0. Nothing migrates, and the store schema is unchanged. The shared provider profile should set work_state: store. coxswain-graphs now infers it from a Postgres storage_url, so setting it explicitly is needed only for older harnesses. Lane hosts on macOS now work for chair duty. The chair publishes its plan meter and its status line to the store and lane hosts read them, so upgrade the chair's machine and the lane hosts together. Restart the chair loop after upgrading cox.

Status: beta. This release finishes the coxtop canvas, adds run history and run cost to coxtop, and makes lands harder to strand. It carries four headlines.

coxtop matches the canvas. Both pages take the canvas's truecolor palettes, with a nearest xterm-256 fallback when the terminal is not truecolor. The Regatta page gets the canvas layout and its restyled frames: the chair line, spend meters with a gradient and a stop tick, machines with lane blocks, a 24-hour lane chart, runs, the queue, the inbox and a key bar. Slipstream gets its run cards and right rail.

Run history and run cost in coxtop. The feed carries ended runs from the store and each run's cost series. coxtop draws a history frame of ended runs with their outcome, cost and PRs, a run-cost frame that graphs each running run's cumulative cost against today's spend, and each lane's stage cost.

Lands that do not strand. A run that loses its store connection retries its exit writes, and the chair marks a run lost when its host is up but its process is dead, so the initiative relaunches. A phase land treats an item already done elsewhere as satisfied, and a refused land blocks only its own initiative. A pytest check that collects no tests is skipped at land. The chair stops relaunching an initiative whose ready task waits on an approved task in the same phase, and decompose now splits such an edge into its own phase. A task whose self-modification review PR merges lands through the chair.

The chair on several machines. The chair machine's lanes can be reserved for decomposes (policy.dispatch.local_lanes: decompose), so builds go to lane hosts. A chair with no plan meter of its own reads the newest meter row from the store, so a standby chair on another machine paces from the real meter. cox stats models compares models per role, and the crew gains a model steward seat that proposes each role's model from those stats.

Upgrading from 0.27.1. Nothing migrates, and the store schema is unchanged. Restart the chair loop and any standby chair after upgrading cox. To keep the chair machine for decomposes, set policy.dispatch.local_lanes: decompose in the team cartridge and give that machine a lane in the hosts table. Two coxtop items move to a later release: the chair panel's integration with the dash, and the Enter and close keys that start and close a session from it.

Status: beta. This release has one headline, and the umbrella's install docs follow it: git and curl are the prerequisites, and uv downloads a managed Python 3.14 when the system one is older.

Python 3.14 is the supported floor. Every Python component requires Python 3.14 or newer, every CI job runs on 3.14, and the old 3.12 floor job becomes a non-blocking 3.15 canary. Coxswain installs through uv tool and the Homebrew tap, which bring their own interpreter, so most installs need nothing new.

Upgrading from 0.28.0. Reinstall with uv tool install --python 3.14 (or uv tool upgrade), which fetches a managed 3.14 if the machine has none. Rebuild any development virtualenv on 3.14. The store schema is unchanged and nothing migrates.

Status: beta. This release lets coxtop act, and gives the queue an order you set. It carries four headlines.

coxtop acts. coxtop runs actions as cox commands: it shows the command it will run and asks you to confirm it first. A colon palette takes a command by name, the footers on every page and drill-down list the keys that work there, and a status line reports the result in the footer row. The chair panel is wired into the app, ready for the render that comes next.

An inbox for what waits on you. cox inbox lists the drafts, approvals and pull requests that need a person.

Priority sets the launch order. Work items carry a priority in the store, and cox route priority <initiative> --set N | --up | --down moves an initiative up or down. The chair launches ready initiatives by priority, then by initiative id.

Lane hosts keep their harness current. A remote launch also brings the lane host's harness checkout up to date. A run that dies because its harness is older than the store's schema is recorded with that cause, and the chair stops relaunching it instead of looping.

Upgrading from 0.29.0. The store gains a priority column (migration 12). The first harness that opens the store migrates it and backs it up with pg_dump first; if pg_dump is not on PATH, back the store up yourself and set COX_STORE_MIGRATE_WITHOUT_BACKUP=1 for that one command. Update coxswain-graphs on every lane host right after the migration. Two coxtop items move to a later release: the chair panel's render and its Enter and close keys. The inbox's needs-chair and refused sources wait on a storage design.

Cut on 2026-10-05. Status: beta. This release makes coxtop the place you run Coxswain from, and lets the chair run with less hand-holding. It carries four headlines. Coxswain's own CI check jobs now read their runner from the COXSWAIN_RUNNER repository variable, so they can move to a self-hosted runner while GitHub-hosted runners are down (coxswain #230, coxswain #231).

coxtop is the entry point. Bare cox on a terminal opens coxtop. The settings screen reads and writes the team cartridge and the hosts table, coxtop adds a machine and edits initiatives, and cox route edit and cox route remove change or drop a filed initiative. The chair panel hosts a Claude session beside the pages: the backtick key opens and hides it, and an ended session frees its keys. Dash releases attach prebuilt coxtop binaries.

coxtop reads the fleet from the store. The chair frame reads the chair's tick from the store, so it shows the loop's health from any machine, with its tick age. The runs list says how each run ended, history marks an idle run as idle instead of crashed, every Regatta frame carries its number, and a run drill-down opens even when the store has not placed the run on a machine yet.

The chair steers clear and carries. The chair holds back a launch whose surfaces overlap a live run, carries a stranded or split phase to its land, gives a free local lane one decompose with no pairing, and skips a lane host whose login has lapsed instead of fetching from it.

Keys that do one thing. Layout cycles on v, so p is only run pause; selection is arrows only, so k is only kill; and Slipstream follows the t theme.

Upgrading from 0.30.0. Nothing migrates, and the store schema is unchanged. Restart the chair loop after upgrading cox, so it writes the chair tick that coxtop now reads. The policy.dispatch.local_lanes: decompose reservation is no longer needed; remove it from the team cartridge. coxtop's watch, spend and health views are partly built (their schemas, stubs and boards are here) and open in 0.32.0.

Cut on 2026-10-06. Status: beta. This release makes coxtop home: the curses screens are gone, and every view they had now lives in coxtop. It also hardens the chair across machines after a night of running it from the Mac, and carries the first parts of 0.33's follow-ups. The umbrella's README and docs landing page show coxtop (coxswain #236), and the crew dashboard gains its cost and quarantine datasets (coxswain #234, coxswain #235).

coxtop is home. cox home, cox console, cox runs top and cox setup open coxtop on a terminal and keep their --once and subcommand forms for scripts. The curses screens and their tests are deleted, and a test fails if any module imports curses again. coxtop gains watch, spend and health drill-downs (w, $, h), fed by schema-1 spend and health snapshots from cox dash --detail. The chair pane releases focus with Ctrl-] or a click on another frame, shows the release key in its title, and Shift+Enter types a newline. coxtop adds and edits initiatives, and listings and the dash feed show short ids beside slugs.

The chair holds across machines. The chair carries a stranded or split phase to its land and rebases a phase branch that fell behind main. A run on the chair's own host homes there; a fetched remote run's store-held approvals keep their run beside a local record, so they land instead of waiting on the chair; a phase land resumes from a pull request it already opened. The store keeps every column a state write leaves out, the stranded check follows a task that moved phase, and a deletion is no longer refused as a change outside its surfaces.

First parts of 0.33. The chair detects a stall when lanes idle with work waiting, pauses lands while the forge's CI is down, and waits for every required check before merging. Needs-chair rows keep their reason and remedy in the store, the chair loop beats its own lease, cox settings validates before writing, and the chair reads lane stats to propose host lanes. A decompose-only chair hands homed work to a lane host.

Upgrading from 0.31.0. Nothing migrates, and the store schema is unchanged. Restart the chair loop after upgrading cox; start it with env -u FORCE_COLOR when it runs under a shell that forces colour, or lands fail the help-snapshot checks. The chair machine's lane count comes from its hosts-table row (cox host capacity).

Cut on 2026-10-06. Status: beta. This release works the follow-ups and the ideas list from running the chair across three machines. Its headline starts moving the record of intake and tickets into the store: a decompose writes rows and runs on any lane, and a relaunch goes to whichever machine has the most free lanes. The chair stops relaunching while it lands, notices when lanes sit idle with work waiting, waits for every required check, and stops hand-carrying phases whose approved commits never reached the phase branch. A crew dashboard shows each seat's cost, approval rate, verdicts and causes (coxswain #239, coxswain #240).

Toward the store as the only record. A decompose writes its tickets as store rows and runs on any lane. A relaunch goes to the machine with the most free lanes, the chair's own included, and moves off a busy home with a fetch of its branches first. Pure helpers read an initiative's ready tasks from rows. The epic launch and the chair do not export work/ from the store yet: the store holds no initiative rows and some task rows without content, so filling it comes first, in 0.34.

The chair lands what it approves. A phase land gathers its approved tasks' commits when the phase branch is missing them, which was behind most of the hand carries of the 0.32 night. The chair does not relaunch an initiative while one of its phases is landing, detects a stall when lanes idle with work waiting and names the blocker, and waits for every required check before a merge, rerunning a failed job once. A task quarantined on a lane host is quarantined in the store, so the chair no longer relaunches its unchanged ticket.

Runs say how they ended. A run records its outcome at exit, and a run's history label reads that outcome, showing blocked or refused with the reason. Needs-chair rows keep the arbitrated reason and remedy, and the inbox lists them. The chair loop beats its own lease.

Smaller things. cox settings validates before writing and can commit a cartridge change. cox imports each command's module only when that command runs. A lane host's launch gate reads the week's spend from the store, so it no longer refuses at a figure several times the meter's when the meter reading is stale. The coxtop chair pane stays up through drill-downs, and backtick puts focus back in it.

Upgrading from 0.32.0. Nothing migrates, and the store schema is unchanged. Restart the chair loop after upgrading cox, still with env -u FORCE_COLOR under a shell that forces colour. Upgrade lane hosts too: a relaunch may now be placed on any of them, and a lane host's launch gate needs tools #1415 to read the week's spend correctly.

Cut on 2026-10-06. Status: beta. The terminal dashboard is renamed towpath (the bank path coaches cycle along to watch and call to the crew): the binary is towpath, cox home, cox console and cox runs top open it, and a coxtop alias keeps working until 0.37 (coxswain-dash #92, coxswain #244). The store is now the record of every initiative and ticket: launches read from it and the chair exports work/ and intake/ from it on each tick.

towpath. The dashboard was coxtop through 0.33. The release assets are now towpath-<tag>-<target>.tar.gz, holding both binaries; the alias prints one line saying it goes away in 0.37 and then runs as before. Past release notes keep the old name.

The store holds everything. A one-time fill writes an initiative row for every initiative and fills tickets the store held without content; an epic launch reads its initiative from rows and exports the board before reading it; a chair tick that changed rows exports and commits work/ and intake/. Every export first fills the store from the files, so a decompose's fresh tickets are never deleted, and an export on a store it cannot read writes and deletes nothing. An intake whose initiative exists is stored as decomposed.

Lands that finish. A phase land updates a pull request that fell behind main and waits for its checks again; it re-reads a merge state GitHub has not computed yet and stops only on a conflict, a missing review or a draft; it reads the PR state from inside the repository; and it takes a task approved in an earlier run of the initiative into the land. The chair keeps relaunches off decompose-only local lanes, knows the quarantined state, posts a daily tier proposal to the inbox, and sends an intake whose decompose wrote nothing twice to the chair instead of decomposing it again.

Started, not yet wired. The parts of reverting a land that turns main red (the rule, its facts and the revert executor) and the notifier's core (off until a channel is configured) are on main; their wiring lands in 0.35. The release tool dispatches an install-proof workflow before merging the tap; until that workflow lands, the tap pull request is left open for a hand merge.

Lands that never drop work. A phase land gathers every task approved for the phase, from this run or an earlier one, and refuses to squash a phase branch that is missing one; a task is marked done only once its commit is on main. Every quarantine in an epic run reaches the store, a conflicting phase merge included. A task approved and then quarantined for its code or its ticket no longer blocks its own relaunch. A timed-out post-land smoke check is inconclusive rather than a red main.

A red main is reverted. After a land, the chair watches main's checks; when they fail, it opens a revert pull request for that land and quarantines the initiative, and two reverts in a row stop its relaunches.

Cut on 2026-10-07. Status: beta. The operations release, and the start of the feature freeze before 1.0: from here on only defects, hardening and docs. The store is backed up daily to Garage and a monthly drill proves a restore, the notifier pushes needs-you events and milestones to a phone, brew install brings towpath along with cox, the model tiers follow the newest model in each family, and the chair stops relaunching work it cannot build.

Operations. A daily job dumps the store, uploads the dump to the Garage bucket the lake already uses and keeps 14 days; a monthly drill restores the newest dump into a scratch database and compares row counts with the live store. The notifier's chair wiring is in, so a configured notify: channel (ntfy) receives needs-you events and milestones. The Forgejo forge is wired: a repository whose origin is on the configured Forgejo host lands through it. The tap step writes the towpath download into the formula, so the next brew upgrade cox installs towpath and coxtop too (coxswain #256).

Models. The provider tiers name model families (haiku, sonnet, opus) and the loader resolves each to the newest catalog row in its family, so a new model needs one catalog row and no tier edit. A refresh lists the vendor's models and reports one newer than the catalog. The standard tier moved to Sonnet 5.5.

A chair that does not spin. An initiative whose repository has a land in flight is not launched, a land the forge refuses backs off instead of being re-planned every tick, and an initiative is capped at a few launches an hour, with one note when a relaunch keeps ending the same way. An epic run reports paused and awaiting_land through its exit code instead of quarantining, a session limit inside any node pauses the run, and an OAuth refresh race between two runs on one machine is retried as a harness fault. A dry-run tick takes about 25 s instead of about 108 s.

To arm the backup on the store host, run ops/store-backup/install.sh from coxswain-tools. If you installed towpath with cargo, the brew copy lands in Homebrew's bin; keep whichever comes first on your PATH.

Cut on 2026-10-11. Status: beta. The first release after the feature freeze: it fixes the defects the 2026-10-07 bug scan found and hardens the chair loop, so a stuck land, a hung call or a dead feed no longer stalls the queue.

A loop that does not hang. Calls on the chair's tick path and its store connections carry timeouts, a refused land retries on a bounded back-off, and the repository land lease is renewed for as long as the land runs. The red-main revert reruns a flaky check before it reverts and never leaves the checkout on its branch. A land's wait for checks sees a startup failure and bounds a required check that never appears.

Runs. Store writes during a run are retried, and network calls in a run time out and kill their process group. A test failure outside a ticket's surfaces is a ticket cause that names the files. Decompose sizes an intake first, so a one-ticket intake becomes one task.

Deferred to 0.38.0. Two quarantined tasks of the login check (host-doctor-local-branch and login-check-evidence-and-two-strikes); the release fetching before it tags; the chair service unit's doctor PATH row; the runs STATUS chip's remaining task; the release notes' cheap opener; and the claude runner's process-group kill.

Upgrading from 0.36.0. Nothing migrates and the store schema is unchanged. Restart the chair loop. A cartridge may list repositories under epic_threshold.inline.repos to let the chair work a change of at most epic_threshold.inline.files_max files inline; the list is empty by default, so nothing changes until you opt in.

Cut on 2026-10-12. Status: beta. Coxswain now ships with no personal references: no person's name, host, home path or private address in any shipped repository, and the release refuses a component whose tree names one. Personal setup lives in two places outside the shipped code: a team cartridge, kept in a repository of its own, and the provider profile. The human that the courier and decisions address is now a profile setting, operator, not a name compiled into cox. The release also unsticks the loop: a phase with a quarantined task still lands its approved tasks, a hand edit to a ticket reaches the store instead of being reverted by the next export, and the loop's store calls cannot hang a tick.

Nothing personal ships. The release runs the clean check, .github/check_clean.py, on every tree it would tag, a pinned component at its tag, and refuses before it cuts. The check refuses home paths, .lan hosts, tailnet and 192.168 addresses, and tracker and platform vendors, and it reads the names to refuse from the COXSWAIN_CLEAN_DENY secret, so the names themselves are never committed. The install guide has a section on where personal setup goes, and the providers page describes the operator.

Lands that keep moving. The chair lands the approved tasks of a phase that also holds a quarantined task, one task at a time, keeps the sibling branches each land would remove, and skips a task another machine has already landed. A land renews its repository lease while it waits on checks. A store-mode fetch of a run with nothing approved succeeds.

The queue says what it means. Route priority can put an initiative on top of or below every other open initiative, measured against open work only. A ticket edited by hand is not overwritten by the export, and cox route edit writes a task ticket to the store first.

A tick that cannot hang. The loop's store connections carry connect, keepalive and statement timeouts. The facts stage has a wall-clock bound; a tick that overruns it is abandoned, and cox chair run exits for its supervisor after three overruns in a row.

A red main from a job that never started is rerun. When main goes red because a CI job never started, the loop reruns it instead of reverting the land that preceded it; a real test failure is still reverted.

Deferred to 0.39.0. The reach allow-list, home-relative repository paths, and an epic land that closes its tasks' review pull requests (the forge call and the selection core land here; the land does not call them yet).

Upgrading from 0.37.0. The store schema is unchanged. Courier rows and decisions are addressed to the profile's operator, which defaults to operator. An install whose courier rows were addressed to a person's name sets operator: <name> in its provider profile, then restarts the chair loop. cox settings get --json reports operator_only and, for this release only, the old pat_only field with the same value; the dashboard reads either. A fork that runs the clean check in CI sets its own COXSWAIN_CLEAN_DENY secret; without it the names rule is skipped and the other rules still run. coxswain-crew rejoins lockstep and is tagged v0.38.0.

docs.text:
• No operator, host or personal path ships: comments keep their reason without a name or date, design docs name the approver by role, and examples and fixtures use neutral hosts and paths (graphs #759). The README drops the link to the removed provenance page (graphs #758).
  • store_cli host login records a host's login state without touching its beat time (graphs #750, graphs #752).
  • The claude runner kills its whole process group on a timeout (graphs #753).
  • Every quarantine records its cause, and a crash in a later phase keeps the earlier phases' approvals (graphs #755).

docs.title: coxswain-tools
docs.text:
• The provider profile's operator key, default operator, names the human the courier and decisions address. cox settings get --json reports operator_only in place of pat_only, and keeps pat_only as an alias for one release (tools #1558).
  • Tests and fixtures use neutral names, and .github/check_clean.py refuses home paths, .lan hosts, tailnet and 192.168 addresses, vendors, and the names in the COXSWAIN_CLEAN_DENY secret (tools #1554). It takes --skip RULE and never scans target/ (tools #1557).
  • A phase with a quarantined task still lands its approved tasks: the chair plans a partial land, lands each approved task in order while it backs up and restores the sibling branches, and the status line names it as partial-land (tools #1529, tools #1543, tools #1544, tools #1545). A task land adopts an open pull request (tools #1545), and a partial land skips a task another machine already landed (tools #1556).
  • The loop's store calls cannot hang a tick: its store connections carry connect, keepalive and statement timeouts (tools #1549), the facts stage has a wall-clock bound (tools #1546), and cox chair run exits 3 after --max-overruns overruns in a row, three by default (tools #1551).
  • Ticket edits reach the store: the export refuses to overwrite a hand-edited ticket, the status line has an item for a ticket file ahead of the store, and cox route edit accepts a task ticket id (tools #1522, tools #1523, tools #1540).
  • cox route priority --top and --bottom place an initiative one above or one below every other open initiative, measured against open work only, and a queued intake takes a priority as well (tools #1524, tools #1527, tools #1531). Decomposed tasks inherit their intake's priority (tools #1547).
  • A red main from a CI job that never started is rerun instead of reverted: the job classifier, the rules, a per-commit read of main's CI, the green-since reader, the facts, the executor's rerun port, and a revert that replaces its own leftover branch (tools #1520, tools #1521, tools #1534, tools #1538, tools #1539, tools #1541, tools #1542). The loop wires the green-since reader and the rerun port, and a pending watch resolves once main goes green at or after its commit (tools #1559); an end-to-end test covers the rerun, the revert and no walk-back (tools #1560).
  • Clearing branches before a relaunch ignores another initiative's lands in the same repository, so a relaunch is not starved by them (tools #1561).
  • The forge can close pull requests, and a pure core picks an epic land's task review pull requests to close (tools #1548).
  • A land renews its repository lease while it waits on checks (tools #1535).
  • A store-mode fetch of a run with nothing approved succeeds, and a failed fetch keeps cox's verdict ahead of git's output in the reason (tools #1532).
  • The login check reads claude auth status from stdout only, renews an expired access token once before it counts a failure, and blocks a host only on its second failure in a row; cox host doctor runs directly on the loop's own host (tools #1528, tools #1530).
  • cox setup doctor checks the chair service unit's PATH: every entry absolute, and cox and pytest reachable (tools #1526). It warns when a model tier is not its family's newest, or the vendor has a newer model than the catalog (tools #1552).
  • Route lint's grant rule flags only the commands a ticket asks the seat to run (tools #1553).
  • The verdict the chair's launch gate will use to launch an initiative only when it has a runnable task (tools #1533).
  • Read-only store connections autocommit, so a read never holds a transaction open, and the notifier backs off and reconnects after a store error instead of exiting (tools #1525).
  • The lake doctor reports a dangling metadata pointer, and housekeeping skips the prune when traces live in object storage and keeps a failed step's last exception line (tools #1536, tools #1537, tools #1555).
  • The load-sensitive CLI startup tests run only when COX_RUN_LOAD_TESTS=1, so a busy host no longer fails a land at random (tools #1550).

The umbrella's tests drop their last personal names (coxswain #289).

Cut on 2026-10-13. Status: beta. This release hardens the chair loop after a night of hand-finished lands. A land that stops records why, a land retries a pull request branch that fell behind main, reuses an empty leftover branch, and lands a one-task run task by task. Export holds are scoped to their own initiative and measured against this workspace's own baseline. Route lint checks that a ticket's surfaces exist, and cox route file resolves a bare repository name. A standby chair pulls the workspace before it takes the lease, the chair paces its lanes against the weekly meter, and a launch skips a lane host whose checkout environment is stale. In the harness, an epic never marks a task approved when its work is on no surviving branch, earned-autonomy streaks come from the store, and an intake can allow a deploy path past the reach lint. The install proof's negative control now installs the real sdist and must fail at its version check, so a green control shows the checks run (coxswain #293).

Lands that say why they stopped. A stopped phase land records its reason, a squash conflict goes to a rebase, and a green pull request a stopped land left behind is adopted. A land updates a behind branch and retries the merge, and an approved task whose run left no phase record lands task by task instead of being refused every tick.

Holds that block only their own initiative. The export guard lists each held file with its initiative, compares a ticket against this workspace's last export and its committed blob rather than the shared store's hash, and baselines the files other harness writers produce. A hold reaches the chair once, and a quarantine in the store always surfaces.

A chair that keeps pace. The chair scales its lane cap by the weekly pace ladder: the weekly spend is compared with a target that grows across the week, and lanes drop to a half, a quarter or none as the spend runs ahead of it.

Deferred to 0.40.0. Home-relative repository paths in work records.

Upgrading from 0.38.0. The store schema is unchanged. Three defaults change. The weekly pace ladder is on: by default the target is 90% of the weekly meter by the week's end, and runs/policy.pacing.json takes weekly_target_fraction and weekly_pace_lanes to tune it. A launch skips a lane host whose checkout environment does not match that repository's uv.lock; run uv sync --frozen --all-extras in that checkout, and the next beat records it. cox setup doctor's chair unit PATH row now also requires claude and uv. cox route file --repo takes a bare repository name or an absolute path and refuses anything else, such as an owner/name. The 0.38.0 manifest kept coxswain-cartridges and coxswain-graphs pinned at v0.37.0 although both were tagged v0.38.0, so an install from the 0.38.0 manifest receives their 0.38.0 and 0.39.0 changes together with this release.

docs.title: coxswain-graphs
docs.text:
• An intake or an idea can carry reach_allow, a list of path prefixes such as a deploy path that the reach lint accepts outside the repository, and decompose runs the reach lint on the idea before its first model call (graphs #761, graphs #771).
  • An epic never marks a task approved when its work is on no surviving branch: the move to approved needs a kept branch, and an end-of-run audit checks every approved task (graphs #767, graphs #773).
  • Earned-autonomy streaks come from the store, not a per-host file, and epic and single-graph runs pass the store to the policy split (graphs #765, graphs #774).
  • A run that dies on a lane host releases its stale worktree holder, and an epic clears a dead run's phase worktree before it reopens the phase, recording what it cleared (graphs #766, graphs #775).
  • A test that polls /proc counts an entry reaped between open and read as gone, which fixes an intermittent CI failure (graphs #770).

docs.title: coxswain-tools
docs.text:
• A stopped phase land records why in its needs-chair row, routes a squash conflict to a rebase instead of a retry, and adopts a green pull request the stopped land left open (tools #1599, tools #1611, tools #1616).
  • A land whose pull request branch is behind main updates the branch and retries the merge instead of stopping (tools #1609).
  • A land reuses an empty leftover pull request branch instead of refusing, and recreates a leftover branch whose cherry-picked tree cannot be computed when it holds no commits that are not on main (tools #1604, tools #1618).
  • An approved task whose run left no phase record, as a one-task run does, lands task by task (tools #1621).
  • A partial land keeps an approved task's run while a newer run of the initiative is live or unfetched, and a cherry-pick conflict stops the task land once with a needs-chair row naming the conflicting paths (tools #1576).
  • A landed task's open review pull requests are closed after the task is marked done, naming the landing commit or pull request, and their branches are deleted (tools #1574).
  • Export holds are scoped and baselined: the guard returns every held file with its initiative from the writer's own predicate (tools #1580); the hand-edit guard compares against this workspace's committed blob and its own export record, never the store's hash (tools #1573); files other harness writers produce are baselined, a hold reaches the chair once, and a store quarantine always surfaces (tools #1622). A ticket's priority stays an integer through the export (tools #1575).
  • A failed route launch records cox's refusal ahead of its stderr warnings (tools #1619).
  • Route lint checks that each surface a ticket names exists in the repository's checkout, and that a surface marked (new) does not exist yet (tools #1589, tools #1598, tools #1610).
  • cox route file --repo resolves a bare repository name to its checkout beside the workspace, keeps an absolute path, and refuses anything else (tools #1577).
  • A standby chair pulls the workspace before it takes the lease, and a live chair run pulls each tick and pushes after an export commit (tools #1582, tools #1590).
  • The weekly pace ladder: a pure verdict compares the weekly spend with a target that grows across the week (tools #1584), the chair's limits scale the launch cap by it (tools #1587), and the feed and the status line carry the target and the verdict (tools #1592, tools #1594, tools #1602).
  • The chair launches an initiative only when it has a runnable task: ready tasks carry their phase, a blocked initiative is withheld, and the status line shows a waiting initiative with its blocking phase (tools #1585, tools #1588, tools #1567, tools #1595).
  • The lane-host environment check: the beat records each checkout's environment against its uv.lock, cox host doctor shows a row per repository with the sync command, and a launch skips a host whose checkout is stale or never synced for that repository and tells the chair once (tools #1603, tools #1605, tools #1607, tools #1615, tools #1617).
  • cox setup doctor's chair unit PATH row checks for claude and uv as well as cox and pytest (tools #1613).
  • A run with an expired lease, no end time and no live process is reported lost (tools #1565).
  • Run rows in the dashboard feed carry how each run ended (tools #1579, tools #1583).
  • cox stats chair, cox stats roles and cox stats efficiency count lands from the store, and efficiency prints where its lands came from (tools #1563, tools #1564, tools #1571). On a Postgres store the gate and efficiency reports read the analytics snapshot (tools #1572).
  • cox --version and the host beat read a checkout-aware version, so an editable install reports its checkout (tools #1566, tools #1570).
  • The parquet doctor tests no longer read the host's chair unit, and uv.lock is relocked for the 0.38.0 version (tools #1596, tools #1608).

Cut on 2026-10-16. Status: beta. The first part of the 0.40 line makes the pieces a second machine depends on work as one system. Work records name their repository relative to the home directory, so a record means the same thing on every host. cox setup --store shared offers a Postgres run store with Garage traces, and cox setup store switch moves between that and files. A chair session attaches to a live loop instead of taking the chair, and project cards link to store rows by key. The towpath view of the chair's background agents follows in 0.41.0, and a dedicated home directory for the install in 0.42.0.

Records that mean the same on every machine. A work record carries a home-relative repository path. The harness expands a tilde-prefixed repository and decompose writes the tilde form, the remote fetch and launch map it for each host, and route lint and the stranded reader expand it. cox route paths lists the stored absolute paths that can be rewritten and --apply rewrites them.

A store shared between machines. cox setup --store shared writes a shared-store.yaml profile that keeps run records in Postgres and traces in an S3-compatible object store such as Garage, and cox setup store switch copies the existing store and traces to the other backend in either direction, leaving the source in place. The setup doctor checks the chosen store. The switch reads the store copier's real per-table output, so a completed copy is not reported as unverified.

Cards that follow the store. A project card links to a work item by key, and the card's status follows the store. cox route file refuses a title that duplicates an open issue unless --force is given, and board items become intake candidates. An initiative can build on one card branch and open one pull request per repository.

The model clamp. A chair records its model, the launcher passes it to the harness, and the runner lowers a seat that would run above it. The clamp is off by default.

docs.title: coxswain-tools
docs.text:
• Work records carry a home-relative repository path: a helper, the remote fetch and launch maps, route lint, the stranded reader, the chair readers, the command edges and the chair exec all expand it (tools #1640, tools #1646, tools #1650, tools #1651, tools #1652, tools #1656, tools #1661, tools #1672).
  • cox route paths lists stored absolute repository paths and --apply rewrites them to the home-relative form (tools #1662, tools #1677).
  • cox setup --store offers the shared store (Postgres run records, S3-compatible traces) and cox setup store switch moves between files and shared: the choice core and profile writer, the setup flag, doctor rows, and a switch verb in each direction (tools #1659, tools #1667, tools #1671, tools #1674, tools #1684). The switch engine reads the copier's real output (tools #1687).
  • cox chair attach says whether a live loop holds the lease and exits 0 if so, and bare cox attaches to a live loop and leaves the lease alone (tools #1670, tools #1678, tools #1689).
  • A chair record carries an optional model, set by cox route chair take --model, and the launcher exports it as COXSWAIN_CHAIR_MODEL (tools #1683, tools #1685, tools #1690).
  • Project cards link to work items by key: a codec and a contract fixture, route pull dedupes, route sync sets a card's status from the store, cox route file refuses a duplicate title, and board items become intake candidates (tools #1655, tools #1680, tools #1686, tools #1692, tools #1693).
  • An initiative builds on one card branch and opens one pull request per repository (tools #1653, tools #1657, tools #1666, tools #1676).
  • cox upgrade moves crew, dash and the umbrella checkout along with the other components, and cox versions words why components can look drifted and when a pin cannot be met (tools #1645, tools #1660, tools #1663).
  • The workspace pull carries the loop's own unstaged files through with --autostash, so a live chair's pull no longer fails every tick (tools #1682).
  • Route lint resolves an initiative id, and route sync reads the active GitHub login and accepts an issue number a land wrote quoted (tools #1654, tools #1679, tools #1691).
  • The lane-host login check sees a token-authenticated host, and the Claude auth status parse tolerates login-shell startup noise (tools #1648, tools #1668, tools #1675).
  • The PR footer drops the coxswain version, and the setup doctor's model-freshness check no longer crashes (tools #1641, tools #1658).

docs.title: Known gaps
docs.text: The store switch is tested against an injected copier and the copier's real output shapes, but it has not been run against a production store. The towpath activity fixture (tools #1694) is groundwork for 0.41.0 and has no reader yet.

docs.title: Components
docs.text:
coxswain-cartridges, coxswain-dash, coxswain-graphs and coxswain-tools change. coxswain-crew is unchanged since v0.38.0 and stays pinned there.

Upgrading from 0.39.1. Nothing to migrate for most installs. The model clamp does nothing by default: it is on only when the chair takes the lease with --model, and each lane host's provider profile needs chair_ceiling_exempt (for example the judge roles validate_phase, arbitrate and review_adversary) before you turn it on, because a lane host reads its own profile. To move an existing install to a shared store, run cox setup store switch shared; cox setup store switch files moves back. cox route paths lists stored absolute repository paths and --apply rewrites them. The Claude Code provider profile now pins the build role to the standard tier.

Cut on 2026-10-16. Status: beta. Towpath now shows the chair's background agents and splits spend between the chair, its agents and the cox seats. The install and upgrade path is repaired after the first clean-machine rehearsal of 0.40.0, an install and an upgrade in a throwaway container: cox install clones components under the names its setup step reads, cox upgrade --to takes each component's pin from the target release, and the install page now gives the commands, flags and steps that work on a clean machine (coxswain #303, coxswain #306). A group of chair and routing fixes ships beside them. The first pieces of a dedicated home directory for the install are in place but wired to no command, and the directory itself ships in 0.42.0. A release rehearsal design and a dispatch-only rehearsal workflow also landed in this repository (coxswain #304, coxswain #305); the workflow cannot gate a release yet, as the known gaps explain.

Towpath shows the chair's background agents. The towpath feed gains a chair_agents section, one row per background agent the chair launched, with its label, model, state, start and finish, tokens and cost. It also gains a spend_split section that divides the five-hour and weekly windows between the chair session, the chair's agents and the cox seats, with each window's meter fraction and reset time. Towpath draws them as a Chair agents frame and a spend split frame on the regatta page, both hidden until toggled with 0 and .. A feed from an older cox carries neither section, and the frames then say there is nothing to show.

An install and upgrade path that works on a clean machine. The first clean-machine rehearsal of 0.40.0, a fresh install and an upgrade from 0.39.1 in a throwaway container, failed both. cox install cloned each component to <root>/<name> while its own setup step read <root>/coxswain-<name>, so the setup step failed. Install now clones to the names setup reads, and fetch, checkout, cox versions and cox upgrade read the same directories. With --to, cox upgrade overrode every component's tag with the target version, which left a pinned component such as crew behind. It now takes each tag from the target release's manifest. The first upgrade run crashed on a module import after its setup step replaced the tool's own environment; install and upgrade now import every module before that step. Install and upgrade exit 0 when only the closing doctor reports failing rows, and print a line that says to create the workspace folders and team cartridge and run cox setup doctor. cox install still does not create those folders or the cartridge, so the install page lists them as steps.

Chair and routing fixes. cox route requeue queues the intake of an initiative whose decompose produced no tasks. cox route file records a repository under the home directory in the tilde form, cox runs cause finds a task whose ticket moved phase after the run, and a relaunch honours lane capacity zero. The land back-off gains a rule that releases a window when the phase branch has a new head; nothing records or passes a head yet, so the back-off still runs its full window.

Groundwork for the home directory, not yet a feature. A design, a location resolver, a setup install plan that can take the resolved locations, and pure migration planners and doctor rows landed. None of it is wired to a command: cox setup migrate does not exist in 0.41.0, cox setup install still lays out under --root, and cox setup doctor does not show the home rows. The directory ships in 0.42.0.

docs.title: coxswain-dash
docs.text:
• The feed reader parses the new chair_agents and spend_split sections against a shared activity fixture. Both are optional, and an agent state it does not know parses as unknown instead of failing the feed (dash #132, dash #133).
  • A Chair agents panel lists each background agent newest first with its state, model, elapsed time, tokens and cost. A spend split panel shows the chair session, chair agents and cox seats in dollars and share for the five-hour and weekly windows, with the meter fraction and the time to reset (dash #134).
  • The regatta page draws both panels in a band under the main frames. 0 toggles the Chair agents frame and . the spend split frame, both hidden by default, and focus cycles through a frame only while it is shown (dash #135).

docs.title: coxswain-tools
docs.text:
• The towpath feed carries the chair's background agents and a three-way spend split. Pure row and split builders (tools #1696) feed readers for the chair session's and agents' transcripts and for the price catalog, with the assembly of both sections (tools #1697), and the feed wiring adds chair_agents and spend_split to the schema 1 snapshot (tools #1698). An agent is done when its last message ends the turn, running while its transcript has moved in the last ten minutes, and failed otherwise, and at most 12 rows are sent.
  • The land back-off rule releases an open window when the refusal recorded a phase branch head and the current head differs. Refusals do not record a head and the land planner does not pass the current one, so no back-off releases on a new head yet (tools #1699).
  • cox route requeue ID queues the intake of an initiative that has no live tasks and drops the empty initiative, so an intake whose decompose produced no tasks can run again. It takes an intake or an initiative, --dry-run, and writes store rows only (tools #1700, tools #1707).
  • cox route file writes a repository under the home directory in the tilde form and expands a --repo ~/... value, so a filing made on the chair machine resolves on every lane host (tools #1701).
  • cox runs cause finds a task whose ticket moved to another phase after the run, by looking for exactly one matching work item in the same initiative (tools #1702).
  • A relaunch honours lane capacity zero: when the local machine and every lane host are capped at 0, no initiative relaunches and the refusal says no lane capacity remains (tools #1703).
  • Groundwork for a dedicated home directory, wired to no command: the design document (tools #1704), a resolver for the home, its installs and workspaces folders, and the config, state and profile paths (tools #1705), a setup install plan that can take the resolved locations and registers the plugin marketplace through the claude command only (tools #1710), and pure planners for moving an existing layout and its lane hosts with doctor rows for the home that cox setup doctor does not show yet (tools #1716).
  • cox install clones each component to <root>/coxswain-<name>, the directory its setup step reads (tools #1706).
  • cox upgrade --to takes each component's tag from the target release's manifest, so a pinned component stays pinned, where it had overridden every component with the target version (tools #1711).
  • The upgrade imports every lazily loaded module before its setup step replaces the tool's environment, so the first upgrade run finishes, and install does the same before its setup step (tools #1708, tools #1712).
  • Install's fetch and checkout, the facts cox versions and cox upgrade gather, and the upgrade runner read each component from its coxswain-<name> directory. A bare directory left by an older install is listed as an extra (tools #1714, tools #1715).
  • Install and upgrade exit 0 when only the closing doctor reports failing rows, and print a line that says to create the workspace folders and team cartridge and run cox setup doctor (tools #1717).

docs.title: Known gaps
docs.text:
The rehearsal landed as a design, a dispatch-only workflow and a script with tests (coxswain #304, coxswain #305), but it cannot gate a release yet. Its fresh and upgrade scenarios download an install.sh that does not exist, so they do not run the documented install, and the release command does not require a passing rehearsal. Requiring it is planned for 0.42.0. The gate for 0.41.0 was a clean-machine rehearsal run by hand in a throwaway Proxmox container. The fresh install and the upgrade from 0.40.0 both passed on tools 4e23473 and the umbrella at 569a119, and the upgrade ran before the tag with the candidate staged in local mirrors.

The home directory and cox setup migrate are 0.42.0. The resolver, the install plan, the migration planners and the doctor rows exist and are tested, but no command calls them. The land back-off does not release on a new head until refusals record one and the planner passes the current one.

docs.title: Components
docs.text:
coxswain-dash and coxswain-tools change. coxswain-cartridges and coxswain-graphs have no commits since v0.40.0 and stay pinned there, and coxswain-crew is unchanged since v0.38.0 and stays pinned there.

Upgrading from 0.40.0. The store schema is unchanged and nothing migrates. Update cox itself first, with uv tool upgrade coxswain-tools or brew upgrade cox, so the upgrade runs with this release's fixes, then run cox upgrade. It takes each component's pin from the 0.41.0 manifest, so crew stays at v0.38.0. An install made with cox install at 0.40.0 has its components cloned under bare directory names (cartridges, graphs, tools, and crew or dash if you installed them), and 0.41.0 reads coxswain-<name>. The upgrade therefore lists each bare directory as an extra and clones a fresh coxswain-<name> beside it at the pinned tag. The bare directories are not upgraded or used again, cox versions keeps listing them as extra, and you can delete them by hand. If you made coxswain-* links to get past the 0.40.0 install failure, the upgrade reads those names and needs no fresh clone.

Cut on 2026-10-17. Status: beta. cox setup migrate moves an existing install under a dedicated home directory, towpath gains a Spend page that breaks spend down by role, tier and model, and a release is now gated on a passing rehearsal of its exact component commits. Every hold that stops the lanes now pushes a notice, after two nights in which one silent hold idled the loop for about nine hours. The land back-off retries a phase as soon as its branch moves, a phase is no longer landed twice, take --steal --model keeps the model, and the install page gives the Python and PATH steps a clean machine needs. Of the home directory promised for this release, only the migration ships: a new install still lays out under --root, as the known gaps explain.

Moving an install under a home directory. cox setup migrate [--home HOME] [--dry-run] [--apply] prints a plan and changes nothing; --dry-run is the same as the default, and only --apply moves anything. The home is --home, then COXSWAIN_HOME, then the recorded home, then $XDG_DATA_HOME/coxswain, then ~/.local/share/coxswain. With --apply it moves the cartridges, graphs and tools checkouts into <home>/installs/ and leaves a link at each old path, points the workspace's base and local cartridge links at the cartridges/<base|local> folders inside the moved checkout, repairs each checkout's git worktrees, rewrites skills_roots, provider_profile and harness_dir in the profile, and records the home in ~/.config/agent-tools/home. A second run reports each step as already done. It never moves the workspace, and it prints, but does not run, the steps it leaves to you: recreating editable installs, registering the plugin marketplace again, and rewriting repository paths with cox route paths. It refuses when no profile setting names a checkout, when cartridges_dir is missing from the profile, or when a destination already exists, and a profile key written as a block-style YAML list cannot be rewritten. After the local steps, each lane host whose heartbeat reports checkouts outside an installs folder gets ssh <host> cox setup migrate --apply, a host already moved has a stale workspace_dir in lane_hosts rewritten, and a host with no heartbeat is listed for you to move by hand. A failed local step stops the run before any host step, and the command exits 1 when any host fails.

A Spend page in towpath. The feed's spend_split section gains two fields in each of its five-hour and weekly windows: by_node, one row per role, tier and model with calls, turns, tokens and cost, most expensive first, and cost_per_landed_task, the window's cox seat spend divided by the tasks landed in it (chair session and chair agent spend are not in it). Only ended runs count. Towpath shows them on a third page, Spend, after Regatta and Slipstream: Tab and Shift-Tab move between pages and f flips the window between five-hour and weekly. The page draws the three-way split, the table, and the cost per landed task; a feed from an older cox shows the split with a line saying it carries no per-role breakdown. Towpath remembers the last page.

A release is gated on a rehearsal. python -m devtools release now refuses to cut unless a release-rehearsal workflow run for the candidate passed: the newest run whose title names each component's current main commit, the previous tag and the declared migrations must have concluded success with its fresh and upgrade jobs green, and its migrate job green when the notes declare a migration. --allow-no-rehearsal REASON cuts without one, and then the notes must carry the line Cut with `--allow-no-rehearsal`: <reason>.. --tap-only skips the gate. The rehearsal workflow runs the install page's own sequence (uv tool install --python 3.14 coxswain-tools, the umbrella clone, cox install --with crew --with dash, the workspace folders, git init, cartridge init) on a clean runner, and its upgrade scenario installs the previous release first.

A refused land retries as soon as its branch moves. The land back-off rule that 0.41.0 added had nothing to read: refusals did not record a head and the planner did not pass the current one, so a refused phase sat out its whole window, up to two hours, even after its branch had been rebuilt. A land now records the tip of its phase branch just before it runs, a refusal carries that head, the chair's facts read the current tip of each refused phase's branch, and the planner passes it in. When the two differ, the window is released and the phase lands on the next tick. A refusal recorded before this release, or a branch that does not resolve, keeps the old full window.

Smaller fixes. cox route chair take --steal --model M records the model when the loop already holds its own lease, where it had been dropped; without --model the recorded model is kept, and the retaken line names it. The install page and README install cox with uv tool install --python 3.14 coxswain-tools, since on an older default Python uv resolved a release from before the 3.14 floor, and they say to run uv tool update-shell and open a new shell when cox is not found. A phase the loop has just landed is no longer planned for a second land on the next tick, and a land that finds its phase branch already gone while every task of that phase is done counts as landed instead of raising a land conflict.

Every hold that stops the lanes reaches you. The notifier had pushed a needs-chair hold only when it was a stranded task or a repeated harness failure, so a ticket or review quarantine could hold the lanes for a night without a word: it happened on 2026-10-16 and 2026-10-17, about nine hours each. Every needs-chair hold now pushes one notice, with its cause, reason and remedy command, through the profile's notify setting, and the existing repeat window keeps it from repeating. A task waiting for another task of its own initiative to land is the normal state of a multi-phase epic and pushes nothing. The idle-stall check now names a blocked task before an empty initiative, and an initiative whose tasks are all finished no longer counts as empty, so its notice names the real blocker instead of a long-finished initiative.
