docs.text: • A third page, Spend, after Regatta and Slipstream, reached with Tab and Shift-Tab. It draws the three-way split, a Role, Tier, Model, Calls, Turns, Tokens and Cost table, and the cost per landed task for the five-hour or weekly window, flipped with f. A feed without the per-role rows shows the split and a line saying so, and the last page shown is remembered (dash #137, dash #138).

docs.title: coxswain-graphs
docs.text: • A build node's run summary keeps a denied list, one entry per tool call that came back refused rather than run, with the tool, its target and the message, so a quarantine can be read after the run's trace is pruned (graphs #795).

docs.title: coxswain-tools
docs.text:
• cox setup migrate plans moving the cartridges, graphs and tools checkouts under the home directory and moves them with --apply, as described above (tools #1719, tools #1722). The workspace cartridge links point at the base and local folders inside the moved cartridges checkout instead of its root (tools #1725).
  • The feed's spend_split windows carry by_node and cost_per_landed_task: a fixture contract (tools #1720), the per-node builder (tools #1721), the activity reader that cuts store rows at each window start (tools #1724), and the feed wiring (tools #1726).
  • cox route chair take --steal --model records the model on a lease its own holder retakes (tools #1723).
  • The approved rows the land planner reads leave out a task the store holds as done, and a land stopped by a missing phase branch whose tasks are all done is recorded as landed, not a conflict (tools #1732).
  • Groundwork for a watchdog that runs outside the loop: its decision rules (loop down on a stale chair lease heartbeat, lanes idle on a hold for a window of status rows) and its store reads and push are in place, but no command calls them yet; cox chair watchdog is planned for 0.43.0 (tools #1730, tools #1733).
  • A land records its phase branch's tip, a refusal keeps it, and the chair reads the current tip of each refused phase and passes it to the land planner, so the back-off releases on a moved branch (tools #1727, tools #1728).
  • Every needs-chair hold pushes a notice with its cause, reason and remedy, except a wait on another task of the same initiative; the idle-stall diagnosis checks blocked tasks before empty initiatives, and an initiative whose tasks are all done or dropped is not an empty one (tools #1729, tools #1731).

docs.title: coxswain
docs.text:
• The release command checks for a passing rehearsal of the candidate's commits and takes --allow-no-rehearsal REASON (coxswain #310).
  • The rehearsal script runs the install page's sequence instead of a missing install.sh (coxswain #309), installs cox on Python 3.14 and puts uv's tool directory on PATH (coxswain #311), and lints the initiative directory it writes, the argument cox route lint takes (coxswain #312).
  • The install page and README pin Python 3.14 for uv tool install and give the uv tool update-shell step (coxswain #311).

docs.title: Known gaps
docs.text:
Only the migration half of the home directory ships. cox install and cox setup install still lay out under --root, so a new install does not use the home until you run cox setup migrate --apply afterwards. The doctor rows for the home, including one that checks the cartridge links, exist but cox setup doctor does not show them, so after a migration it reports what it reported before.

The rehearsal workflow's migrate scenario runs only for a declared migration id, and its mapping from an id to a command is a placeholder; this release declares none. cox setup migrate was rehearsed by hand instead, in a throwaway Proxmox container on the same commits. A dry run changed nothing, --apply moved the checkouts under the home and repointed the profile and the cartridge links, cox setup doctor reported no failing rows, no link or path was left dangling, every work record survived, and a second run changed nothing. The fresh install and the upgrade from 0.41.0 passed both in that container and in the hosted rehearsal (run 39037740345) on tools a061ac0, graphs 304a533, dash 882c528, cartridges 8584e34 and crew 80eb36a.

Migrations: none

docs.title: Components
docs.text:
coxswain-dash, coxswain-graphs and coxswain-tools change, so graphs rejoins the release at 0.42.0. coxswain-cartridges has no commits since v0.40.0 and stays pinned there, and coxswain-crew is unchanged since v0.38.0 and stays pinned there.

Upgrading from 0.41.0. The store schema is unchanged and nothing migrates on its own. Update cox itself first, with uv tool upgrade coxswain-tools or brew upgrade cox, then run cox upgrade. To move an existing install under the home directory, run cox setup migrate to see the plan, then cox setup migrate --apply, and run cox setup doctor afterwards.

Cut on 2026-10-17. Status: beta. Lands can be frozen for a release cut with cox chair freeze-lands while the lanes keep building. A quarantine caused by the ticket or the code is relaunched once by the loop instead of held for the chair, and the relaunched run sends the task to triage before it builds again. cox chair watchdog checks the loop from outside it, run from a five-minute timer. An initiative is marked done on the tick its last task closes, cox runs triage prints a quarantined task's facts in one command, and cox route paths --move swaps a moved repository prefix in the queue rows and work files. The home directory install is still not wired: a new install lays out under --root, and the install into the home moves to 0.44.0, as the known gaps explain.

Freezing lands for a release cut. cox chair freeze-lands --for MINUTES --reason TEXT writes a land-freeze row to the store's leases table that expires after MINUTES. While it stands, the chair plans no phase land and no task land. Fetches, launches and holds are still planned, so the lanes keep building and approved work waits on its branches. The status line gains a lands frozen until HH:MM (reason) part, with the time in UTC. With neither flag the command prints whether lands are frozen, --off lifts the freeze, and a freeze that outlives its minutes lifts itself, so a forgotten freeze never needs deleting. --for and --reason go together and never with --off, MINUTES is at least 1, and any other mix prints the usage line and exits 1.

A ticket or code quarantine is relaunched once. A quarantine whose cause is the ticket or the code held its initiative for the chair. The loop now relaunches it once on the ticket's current body, and a second quarantine on that body reaches the chair with the first and the latest attempt's reasons, 300 characters each. In the relaunched run the epic harness caps a task whose newest attempt was caused by the ticket or the code at one attempt instead of two, so the task goes to triage before it builds again. When triage proposes a ticket amendment that only appends text to the body, the harness applies it at once, without waiting on the approval gate, provided the amendment is eligible and the cartridge names a model apply arm. It then checks that the ticket file holds the old body with text appended, and rebuilds the task on the new body in the same run with its attempt count reset. An apply that fails or writes anything else is undone: the ticket file is restored to the bytes read before, and the task is quarantined with the reason.

A watchdog outside the loop. cox chair watchdog [--idle-minutes N] [--stale-minutes N] [--dry-run] is a one-shot check meant for a five-minute timer. It reads the chair lease and the recent status lines from the store. It pushes Chair loop down when the lease has no row or no beat in --stale-minutes (default 10), or when no status line was written in the last --idle-minutes (default 30). It pushes Lanes idle <minutes> min, naming the holds, when every status line in that window shows no busy lane and at least one hold. It pushes through the profile's notify setting with the loop's own sent-state file, --dry-run prints the alerts and pushes nothing, and it exits 1 only when the store cannot be read. This command and the empty-decompose report below were already in the 0.42.0 packages, though the 0.42.0 notes left them out and called the watchdog planned.

An initiative closes on the tick its last task closes. In store mode, each tick the chair finds every initiative still in state todo whose task rows are all done or dropped, and moves it to done, or to dropped when none of its tasks is done. An initiative with no task rows is left alone, and the close is planned even while a limit has stopped launches.

cox runs triage TASK_ID [--json] prints a quarantined task's facts. It reads the store and git and makes no model call. It prints the task's initiative, phase, state and newest run, each recorded attempt with its kind, cause and reason, the review verdict and its objection, the last failed check with the last 20 lines of its output, the phase's latest land refusal with its time, head and reason, and each surface as present, missing, or new when a surface marked (new) is not on main yet. The store is the one the profile names, and surfaces are looked up on main, else origin/main, of the git repository in the current directory. An unknown task id exits 1 with a line saying so.

cox route paths --move OLD NEW swaps a moved repository prefix. In store mode it rewrites each row's repo and its absolute or tilde surfaces; otherwise it rewrites each work file's repo: line and surfaces. OLD and NEW are taken to the tilde form first, a path moves only when it is OLD or lies under OLD/, and a relative surface never moves. Like the rest of route paths it lists the changes and writes nothing without --apply. With --apply it reads the rows or files again, prints how many values are still under OLD, and exits 1 when any are. It is the step cox setup migrate --apply prints, but does not run, after it moves the checkouts.

cox setup migrate --apply migrates only this machine. In 0.42.0 --apply went on to each lane host after the local steps. The host steps now run only with --apply --hosts, on the chair's machine; without --hosts the command prints a line saying the hosts were not touched.

Smaller fixes. A needs-chair hold now pushes once while it stands. The one-hour repeat window had pushed a standing hold again every hour, 19 notices in 46 minutes on 2026-10-17; its key is now kept while the hold stands and pruned an hour after it clears. Holds the loop clears by itself (a land between its fetch and its record, a launch deferred behind a running initiative that shares a file, a work file the export left alone) never push. A decomposed intake whose decompose run ended with no stored tasks is reported as a hold with cox route requeue <initiative> as its remedy, cox route requeue finds the intake through the intake: field of initiative.md when no store row links them, and an initiative already done or dropped is never reported as an empty decompose. A launch on a lane host syncs the harness and the repository at the checkout of the same name that the host's heartbeat recorded, migrated under installs/ or not, and pushes the repository there. A decompose names its initiative from the intake's title, where it had used the whole intake file, and the ticket lint no longer refuses a path under tests/ as corpus.

docs.title: coxswain-graphs
docs.text:
• A task whose newest attempt was caused by the ticket or the code is capped at one attempt instead of two, so a relaunch sends it to triage before it builds again (graphs #800).
  • An append-only ticket amendment from triage is applied at once when it is eligible and the cartridge names a model apply arm. The written file is checked for the old body with text appended, and the task is rebuilt on the new body in the same run with its attempt count reset. A failed or mismatched apply restores the file and quarantines the task with the reason (graphs #803).
  • A decompose takes its initiative's title from the intake's title:, else its first # heading, else its first line, as one line of at most 120 characters. The intake's frontmatter is dropped from the why, its repo: is used when the launch names no repository, and a title that spans more than one line is refused (graphs #802).
  • The ticket lint reads a path under tests/ as repository code, never corpus, so a ticket naming a folder such as tests/fixtures/help/runs/ is no longer refused at decompose (graphs #798).
  • Tests only: the store DDL tests pin only their own upgrade, and the decompose, tier, handoff and infrastructure tests stop pinning constants, private helpers and prompt wording. They remove 44 tests and add 5, and the suite goes from 2,406 test functions at v0.42.0 to 2,389. No DDL or migration changed (graphs #804, graphs #805, graphs #806, graphs #807).

docs.title: coxswain-tools
docs.text:
• cox chair freeze-lands [--for MINUTES] [--reason TEXT] [--off] sets, shows or lifts a land freeze kept as an expiring land-freeze row in the leases table (tools #1738). The land planner plans no land while it stands (tools #1744), and the status line shows it (tools #1747).
  • A ticket or code quarantine with one attempt on its current body is relaunched, and the second attempt on that body reaches the chair with the first and latest reasons (tools #1742).
  • cox chair watchdog pushes when the loop is down or its lanes sit idle on a hold, as described above. It shipped in the 0.42.0 packages (tools #1735) on the rules and readers that 0.42.0 described as groundwork.
  • A decompose that wrote an initiative with no tasks is reported as a hold with the requeue command as its remedy, and cox route requeue reads the intake from initiative.md when no store row links it. This also shipped in the 0.42.0 packages (tools #1736). An initiative already done or dropped is left out (tools #1739).
  • The chair reads each todo initiative with its task rows' states (tools #1745) and closes one whose tasks are all done or dropped, as done when any task is done and as dropped otherwise (tools #1761).
  • cox runs triage TASK_ID [--json] prints a task's attempts, review, failed check, land refusal and surfaces: the pure core shipped in the 0.42.0 packages (tools #1734), then came the store and git readers (tools #1740) and the command (tools #1754).
  • cox route paths --move OLD NEW swaps a repository prefix in the store rows or work files (tools #1743) and reports what is still under OLD after --apply (tools #1748).
  • A notice is pushed once while its hold stands and pruned an hour after it clears, and the no_run, steer_deferred and held_file holds never push (tools #1741).
  • A launch on a lane host syncs the harness and the repository at the host's recorded checkout of the same name, and maps the harness path to the host's home when it has none (tools #1746). The dry run of a launch on a host lists those sync steps when the host has recorded checkouts (tools #1752).
  • cox setup migrate --apply runs the host steps only with --hosts. The preflight refusals for a held lease, a live lane, the chair's lease and an active host row are written but not called yet (tools #1751).
  • Groundwork for installing into the home, wired to no command: the install plan can create the default workspace <workspaces>/main with its folders and record the home, and a reader lists the installed plugin marketplaces (tools #1750).
  • A renderer and check for the README's commands block now live in this repository, as a module with tests; no command or test outside its own calls it yet (tools #1762).
  • Tests only: six consolidation changes drop tests that pinned defaults, private plumbing and status-line wording, and the fake servers and the chair-run test rig stop waiting idle. They remove 95 tests and add 18, and the CLI dispatch test stops pinning the number of handlers (tools #1749, tools #1755, tools #1756, tools #1757, tools #1758, tools #1759, tools #1760). With the new features' tests, the suite goes from 6,962 test functions at v0.42.0 to 7,001.

docs.title: coxswain
docs.text: • The release rehearsal's fresh scenario installed into the default coxswain home with no --root, and its upgrade scenario ran cox setup migrate --apply after the pin (coxswain #317). Both were reverted for this cut, since cox install at 0.43.0 still requires --root (coxswain #318); they come back with the home install in 0.44.0.

docs.title: Known gaps
docs.text:
The home directory install is still not wired. cox install and cox setup install require --root, so a new install does not use the home until you run cox setup migrate --apply afterwards. The install plan's default workspace and home record and the marketplace reader exist but no command calls them (tools #1750). Wiring them is 0.44.0, and so is the rehearsal that installs fresh into the home. cox setup doctor still does not show the doctor rows for the home.

The cox setup migrate --apply preflight is partial. Only the --hosts split ships. The refusals that should stop --apply while a lease holds a checkout, a lane runs on this machine, the chair holds its lease here, or this host's row is active are written and tested but not called, so drain the host and stop the loop yourself before you migrate.

The empty-decompose hold always says that no refusal line was found in the decompose log, since nothing reads that log for it yet. Nothing records that the hold was reported either, so it is planned again on every tick until the intake is requeued. Since tools #1741 it pushes only once while it stands.

cox runs triage takes no --profile or --repo: it reads the store the routing profile names and looks surfaces up in the repository of the current directory, so run it from the task's repository. cox chair watchdog is installed as a command only; nothing sets up its timer, so add one yourself. Closing an initiative on its last task works in store mode only.

The gate for 0.43.0 was the hosted rehearsal (run 39062083584), whose fresh, upgrade and migrate jobs passed, on tools c1784d3, graphs edd8f74, dash b654297, cartridges 8584e34 and crew 80eb36a, with the umbrella at 281b845. A clean-machine rehearsal in a throwaway Proxmox container passed the fresh install, the upgrade from 0.42.0 and cox setup migrate on tools 2df7632, the commit before tools #1762, which adds a module nothing calls yet. An earlier hosted run with the umbrella at 530285f failed its fresh job (run 39061438425) because that scenario installed with no --root. A land freeze does not stop a land the loop planned before the freeze was set: tools #1762 landed that way during this cut.

Migrations: none

docs.title: Components
docs.text:
coxswain-graphs and coxswain-tools change and are released at 0.43.0. coxswain-dash has no commits since v0.42.0 and stays pinned there, coxswain-cartridges has none since v0.40.0 and stays pinned there, and coxswain-crew is unchanged since v0.38.0 and stays pinned there.

Upgrading from 0.42.0. The store schema is unchanged and nothing migrates on its own; the land freeze uses the existing leases table. Update cox itself first, with uv tool upgrade coxswain-tools or brew upgrade cox, then run cox upgrade. If you move an install under the home directory, cox setup migrate --apply now moves only this machine: run cox setup migrate --apply --hosts on the chair's machine to move the lane hosts too. To use the watchdog, call cox chair watchdog every five minutes from a timer of your own on a machine that can read the store.

Cut on 2026-10-17. Status: beta. The dedicated coxswain home is finished. cox install and cox upgrade without --root lay out under the home's installs folder, cox setup doctor shows the home rows, and cox setup migrate --apply moves an existing install with a preflight that refuses while anything holds a checkout. The migration now recreates the virtualenvs and reinstalls the cox and cartridge uv tools from the moved checkouts, re-registers the coxswain-cartridges plugin marketplace, and regenerates the chair systemd unit on Linux. Once every host has moved, cox setup migrate --finish --apply rewrites the shared repository paths and removes the compatibility links. A machine not yet migrated warns on the home rows instead of failing its doctor, and cox setup install keeps the extras of the cox and cartridge uv tools. A land freeze is re-checked before each land of a running tick, an empty-decompose hold waits for the decompose process to exit, land heads resolve for a repository recorded in tilde form, and cox upgrade --to takes a bare version. The 0.42.0 and 0.43.0 known gaps about the home not being wired are closed, except where the known gaps below say otherwise.

A new install lays out under the home. cox install and cox upgrade no longer require --root. Without it the installs folder is <home>/installs, where the home is --home, then COXSWAIN_HOME, then the recorded home, then $XDG_DATA_HOME/coxswain, then ~/.local/share/coxswain. The manifest is read from <home>/installs/coxswain/ manifest.toml, so the umbrella is cloned there first, and a missing manifest is refused with a line that says so. cox install creates the installs folder before it runs its steps, and its setup step runs cox setup install --home <home> in place of --root. With no --workspace, that step makes the default workspace <home>/workspaces/main with its work, runs, intake and cartridges folders, and its last write records the home in ~/.config/agent-tools/home. cox setup install without --root already laid out under the home in the 0.43.0 packages, though the 0.43.0 notes said it required --root; it still refuses a home named by --home or COXSWAIN_HOME that differs from the recorded one and tells you to run cox setup migrate --home. With --root, all three commands behave as in 0.43.0, and cox setup install --root still requires --workspace.

cox setup doctor shows the home rows. After the install rows and before the store rows, the doctor prints home root, marketplace registered and marketplace location, then old layout, home paths, home recorded, cartridge links and install bins. home root fails when the home is missing or not writable. The two marketplace rows warn, without failing, when claude is not on PATH. home paths passes when every skills root, the provider profile and the harness dir sit under the home after tilde expansion, and home recorded passes when the home record names the resolved home. cartridge links accepts a base or local link that points at its folder under coxswain-cartridges/cartridges in the installs folder, written relative or absolute. install bins compares four editable sources with their checkouts under the installs folder: the graphs and tools virtualenvs, read from each package's direct_url.json, and the cox and cartridge uv tools, read from their receipts in uv tool dir; it is left out when uv tool dir cannot be read. On a machine with no home record, old layout, home paths, home recorded and cartridge links warn not migrated: run cox setup migrate, and a failing home root, marketplace registered, marketplace location or install bins row warns not migrated: run cox setup migrate; <detail> instead of failing, so an install made before 0.44.0 keeps a passing doctor until it is moved. Every row compares text and follows no link, and without a profile every home row is skipped.

cox setup migrate --apply refuses while anything holds a checkout. When the plan holds any step beyond a skip or a print, local or, with --hosts, on a lane host, --apply first takes a one-hour repository lease on each old checkout, held as migrate@<host>:<pid>, and only then reads the live lanes, the chair lease and this host's row in the store's hosts table. It refuses, prints one line per holder and exits 1 when a lease is held by someone else, a live lane runs on this machine, the chair holds a live lease here, or this host's row is active, with cox host drain <host> named as the remedy for the last. It does not wait and stops no run. A preflight that passes writes migrate.json in the coxswain state folder with the old and new checkout roots, and the leases are released when the command ends, whether it moved anything or not. The refusals were written in 0.43.0 and are now called (tools #1766).

The migration recreates the virtualenvs and reinstalls the uv tools. When any of the four editable sources the install bins row checks is not its checkout under the installs folder, the plan gains eight steps after the worktree repair. For coxswain-tools, coxswain-graphs and coxswain-cartridges in that order, it runs uv venv --clear -q and uv pip install -q -e .[dev] in the moved checkout, the graphs install also taking the cartridges checkout editable. It then runs uv tool install --force -q -e on the tools checkout and on the cartridges checkout, each with the extras its uv tool receipt names, so a cox installed with an extra keeps it. When uv tool dir cannot be read the plan has no reinstall steps. Because the reinstall replaces the environment cox runs from, --apply imports every module it may need before the first step runs. The 0.42.0 printed note that left the editable installs to you is gone.

The migration re-registers the plugin marketplace. When claude is on PATH and claude plugin marketplace list shows coxswain-cartridges anywhere but the cartridges checkout under the installs folder, the plan runs claude plugin marketplace remove coxswain-cartridges when an entry exists, then claude plugin marketplace add with the moved checkout. It then runs claude plugin install again for each plugin id ending @coxswain-cartridges that claude plugin list --json lists, or for local-skills@coxswain-cartridges when none is listed. When claude is not on PATH the plan prints that the marketplace was not checked. This replaces the 0.42.0 printed note that left the marketplace to you.

The migration regenerates the chair systemd unit on Linux. On Linux the plan reads coxswain-chair.service from ~/.config/systemd/user, and when its Environment=PATH= line still names a coxswain- checkout under the old root, the plan ends with a chair_unit step; a machine with nothing else left to move gets that step alone. The step reads --label, --interval and --profile back out of the unit's chair run line and the file its EnvironmentFile= names, and rebuilds the unit the way cox chair service --install does, with the cox now on PATH. It writes the unit, runs systemctl --user daemon-reload, and restarts the service only when it was active. A unit with no chair run line, no usable label or interval, or values that the install would refuse is left as it is with a line saying why. A failed systemctl call fails the step.

cox setup migrate --finish closes the move once every host has moved. cox setup migrate --finish [--old-root PATH] [--apply] [--dry-run] is its own mode: it plans by default and changes things only with --apply, and --dry-run keeps it a plan even beside --apply. The old checkout root is --old-root, else the old_root that migrate.json recorded; with neither it prints finish: no old root known; pass --old-root and exits 2. It refuses --hosts, and --old-root without --finish, with exit 2. It first checks its gates and prints one finish: waiting on ... line per gate that fails, exiting 1: this machine's plain migrate plan must be a single skip, every home row of the doctor must pass, and every lane host must have a beat row whose checkouts all sit under an installs folder. With --apply it also refuses, exit 1, while a live lane runs on this machine, the chair holds a live lease here, or this host's row is active, as the plain --apply preflight does. Then, for each of the three checkouts, it rewrites the tilde prefix under the old root to the tilde prefix under the installs folder: in the store's queue rows in store mode, else in the work files, the same rewrite as cox route paths --move. It reads the rows again afterwards and exits 1 with finish: N value(s) still under <old root> when any remain, removing nothing. Only then does it remove each link on this machine at <old root>/<checkout> whose target is exactly that checkout under the installs folder, keeps anything else there with a finish: kept <path>: <reason> line, and deletes the marker. Each change is printed as finish: rewrite, finish: remove or finish: delete the marker, as finish: would ... without --apply, and a machine with nothing left prints finish: nothing to do. A store it cannot read, or a profile that does not say where the queue lives, exits 2 with nothing removed. The plain migrate plan now prints run cox setup migrate --finish once every host has migrated. in place of the note that left the repository paths to you.

The rest of the move shipped in 0.43.0. A launch on a lane host maps the harness to the host's recorded checkout of the same name (tools #1746), so hosts on the old and the new layout run side by side while the fleet moves, and cox route paths --move OLD NEW swaps a moved prefix by hand (tools #1743).

Smaller fixes. A land freeze set while a tick runs now stops the lands that tick had already planned: each land re-reads the freeze at the tick's clock as it starts, and a live freeze skips it with the lands frozen until HH:MM (reason) text and no escalation, for a later tick to plan again. A land already running is not stopped. An empty decompose is no longer reported while the decompose process still runs: the runs row can end before the process has written every item, so an initiative whose newest decompose run has a live process, by its pid file in the runs folder or by the tick's pid probe, is left out. The chair's land facts expand a tilde repository path before reading the tip of a refused phase's branch, which had not resolved for such a path, so a phase recorded with a tilde path kept the full land back-off window after its branch moved. cox upgrade --to 0.44.0 reads the bare version as the tag v0.44.0, where it had looked for a tag named 0.44.0. cox setup install, and so the setup step of cox install and cox upgrade, reads the extras of the installed cox and cartridge tools from their uv receipts (under UV_TOOL_DIR, else $XDG_DATA_HOME/uv/tools, else ~/.local/share/uv/tools) and puts them on its uv tool install -e targets, so a tool installed with an extra keeps it.

docs.title: coxswain-tools
docs.text:
• cox install and cox upgrade take --home, and without --root they install under <home>/installs and pass --home to the setup step (tools #1772, tools #1777).
  • cox setup install creates the default workspace folders under the home, where a run into the home had stopped at its first step with no message, and a stopped run now names the step that stopped it (tools #1787).
  • cox setup install reinstalls the cox and cartridge tools from the checkouts under the home with --force, so a cox first installed from PyPI is replaced and its uv receipt names the checkout (tools #1789).
  • cox setup doctor shows the coxswain home rows: home paths, home recorded and install bins are new, the marketplace rows warn when claude is absent, and an unmigrated machine warns on four rows (tools #1767, tools #1770). The doctor command gathers them (tools #1775). On an unmigrated machine a failing home root, marketplace or install bins row warns instead of failing (tools #1784). On any machine, a coxswain-cartridges marketplace that is not registered at all warns on marketplace registered and marketplace location and names cox setup install --plugins, since the plugins step is optional; one registered at the wrong path still fails (tools #1788).
  • cox setup migrate --apply takes a lease on each old checkout and refuses while a lease, a live lane, the chair's lease or this host's active row holds it, then writes the migration marker (tools #1766).
  • The migration recreates the three virtualenvs and reinstalls the cox and cartridge uv tools with their extras when an editable source is not under the installs folder: the venv steps are shared with cox setup install (tools #1767), the plan builds the eight steps (tools #1769) and --apply observes the sources and runs them (tools #1779).
  • The migration re-registers the coxswain-cartridges marketplace and reinstalls its plugins: the install's marketplace steps are public (tools #1774), the plan adds them (tools #1776) and --apply observes the registry and runs them (tools #1782).
  • The migration regenerates the chair systemd unit on Linux when its PATH names the old root: the plan step and a reader of the unit's arguments (tools #1765), then the step itself, which shares the unit builder with cox chair service --install (tools #1771).
  • cox setup migrate --finish [--old-root PATH] checks that this machine and every lane host have moved, rewrites the repository paths under the old root, then removes the compatibility links and the marker: the lane-host check is public (tools #1780), the pure finishing step (tools #1785) and the command (tools #1786).
  • A land freeze is re-checked before each land of a running tick, and a land it skips is not escalated (tools #1768).
  • An empty-decompose hold leaves out an initiative whose newest decompose process is still alive (tools #1773).
  • Land heads resolve for a repository path written with a tilde (tools #1778).
  • cox upgrade --to accepts a bare version such as 0.44.0, and the setup install plan carries the coxswain-tools extras on its uv tool install target (tools #1781). cox setup install reads the cox and cartridge extras from the uv receipts and passes both (tools #1783).
  • With the new features' tests, the suite goes from 7,018 test functions at v0.43.0 to 7,157.

docs.title: coxswain
docs.text:
• The release rehearsal's fresh scenario installs the candidate tools first, clones the umbrella into the default home's installs folder and runs cox install with no --root or --workspace, and its upgrade scenario runs cox setup migrate --apply after the pin and before the lint. This re-applies coxswain #317, which 0.43.0 reverted (coxswain #322). Its fresh scenario builds the workspace at the home's default workspaces/main, the one the profile names (coxswain #325), and its pin step reinstalls cox editable from the tools checkout at the candidate SHA, the install cox setup install leaves behind (coxswain #326).
  • The install page installs into the home: the umbrella is cloned to <home>/installs/coxswain and cox install runs with no --root, the page says how the home resolves and that --root and --workspace go together, and a new section, Moving an install under the home, gives cox setup migrate, --apply, --apply --hosts and --finish (coxswain #323, coxswain #324).

docs.title: Known gaps
docs.text:
Some of what docs/design/coxswain-home.md promises is not built. The doctor has no lane host paths or migration state row, and profile paths does not check umbrella_dir. The migration marker records only the old and new roots, not the last finished step. The migration does not list operator scripts or launchd jobs that still name an old bin folder, and emits no beat when it ends, so a lane host's row shows the new paths only on its next beat and --finish waits on that beat. The repository paths are rewritten only by --finish, after every host has moved, so until then the queue keeps the old paths and reaches the checkouts through the compatibility links.

From 0.43.0, still open: the empty-decompose hold always says no refusal line was found in the decompose log, and nothing records that it was reported. cox runs triage takes no --profile or --repo, nothing sets up the timer for cox chair watchdog, and closing an initiative on its last task works in store mode only.

The gate for 0.44.0 was the hosted rehearsal (run 39079091745), whose fresh, upgrade and migrate jobs passed, and a clean-machine rehearsal in a throwaway Proxmox container, where the fresh install, the upgrade from 0.43.0 and cox setup migrate passed. Both ran on tools 84647e0, graphs 0c138e2, dash b654297, cartridges 8584e34 and crew 80eb36a. The fresh scenario now installs into the home with no --root. Its earlier runs on this candidate found the three install fixes listed above (tools #1787, tools #1788, tools #1789) and two faults in the rehearsal itself (coxswain #325, coxswain #326).

Migrations: none

docs.title: Components
docs.text:
coxswain-tools changes and is released at 0.44.0. coxswain-graphs has no commits since v0.43.0 and stays pinned there, coxswain-dash has none since v0.42.0 and stays pinned there, coxswain-cartridges has none since v0.40.0 and stays pinned there, and coxswain-crew is unchanged since v0.38.0 and stays pinned there. The umbrella changes its release rehearsal (coxswain #322, coxswain #325, coxswain #326) and its install page (coxswain #323, coxswain #324).

Upgrading from 0.43.0. The store schema is unchanged and nothing migrates on its own. Update cox itself first, with uv tool upgrade coxswain-tools or brew upgrade cox, then run cox upgrade, with --root if your install is not yet under the home. To move an existing install, run cox setup migrate on each machine to see the plan, then cox setup migrate --apply with the loop stopped and the host drained, since the preflight refuses otherwise. Move the lane hosts with cox setup migrate --apply --hosts from the chair's machine, or run cox setup migrate --apply on each host in turn, and check each with cox setup doctor. Once every host has moved and beaten, run cox setup migrate --finish to see what it would rewrite and remove, then cox setup migrate --finish --apply with that machine's lanes and loop stopped. The first machine to finish rewrites the shared repository paths; each machine removes only its own links and marker, so run it on every machine, and pass --old-root on one whose marker is gone.

Cut on 2026-10-18. Status: beta. A chair that cannot reach a shared store lease now refuses the chair instead of falling back to the lock file, which only sees chairs on its own machine. cox setup migrate and cox setup doctor read the chair unit's PATH across its systemd drop-ins as well as the unit file, and the migration rewrites a drop-in that still names the old checkout root. A fetched remote run no longer moves a task that the chair changed after the run started, and cox setup migrate keeps each virtualenv's extras when it recreates it. The test suite drops the byte-for-byte help snapshots and the help-wording tests, and the stats CLI tests pin each decision once. Only coxswain-tools changes.

A chair that cannot reach a shared store lease refuses the chair. When the store is postgres, a lease that cannot be acquired, whether the lease call fails, answers released instead of granted, or finds no harness, now refuses with chair: cannot reach the store lease (<detail>); not taking the chair, and cox chair take exits 2. Before, every one of those cases warned and fell back to the lock file, which cannot see a chair on another machine. During the 0.44 home migration a rebuilt virtualenv on a standby lacked the postgres driver, the lease call failed, and the standby ticked as chair for 17 seconds. The files store keeps the fallback and its warning, since its lock file is the whole truth there. A chair that already holds the lease and fails to renew it still warns and keeps the chair, so one store blip does not abandon a chair in the middle of a land; only acquiring refuses. A chair with no lease sidecar, one taken before the lease existed or one that had fallen back to the lock file, acquires at its next beat and so refuses in the same way (tools #1794).

The chair unit's PATH is read from its drop-ins too. systemd lets a *.conf file under ~/.config/systemd/user/coxswain-chair.service.d/ override the unit's Environment=PATH=, and a machine that set the PATH that way looked fine to the doctor and the migration while the chair ran from the old folders. The effective PATH is now read from the unit file first, then its drop-ins in file-name order, the last one that sets PATH winning (tools #1793). The doctor's chair unit PATH row checks that value, adds (from <file>) to its detail, and fails with no Environment=PATH= line in the unit or any drop-in (both checked) only when neither sets one. In cox setup migrate, when the effective PATH still names a coxswain- checkout under the old root and comes from the unit file, the plan ends with the chair_unit step as in 0.44.0; when it comes from a drop-in, the plan ends with a chair_unit_dropin step that names that drop-in. On --apply that step replaces each old checkout folder with its new one on the drop-in's Environment=PATH= lines, leaves the unit file and every other drop-in alone, runs systemctl --user daemon-reload, and restarts the chair only when systemctl --user is-active said it was running when the plan was made. An unreadable drop-in is left as it is with a line saying so, and a failed systemctl call fails the step (tools #1796).

A fetched remote run never overwrites a task the chair changed after the run started. When the store holds the task records, fetching a remote run moves each task the run approved from ready to approved. It now first compares the task's updated_at in the store with the run's started_at, and a task updated strictly later keeps its state with fetch: <task> kept <state>, changed after run <run> started, so a task the chair edited or requeued while the run was out is not approved from the run's stale outcome. A missing or unparseable timestamp leaves the fetch as it was (tools #1797).

The test suite is lighter. The consolidation that began in 0.43.0 (tools #1755 to tools #1760) continues and removes tests that pinned what development changes on purpose, on the principle that a test which hinders development has lost its value and that functional code is largely self-testing. The byte-for-byte help snapshots are gone: the 101 fixture files under tests/fixtures/help, the snapshot suite that compared every command group's --help with them, and the pytest --regen option that rewrote them (tools #1791, tools #1795). The tests that pinned help wording in the CLI help, chair run, chair holder and beat loop deprecation suites go with them (tools #1791), and the stats CLI tests drop their duplicates so each decision is pinned once (tools #1792). Counted as def test_ lines, the consolidation removes 19 test functions and the new features add 36, so the suite goes from 7,158 at v0.44.0 to 7,175; the snapshot suite alone ran 116 parametrized cases. The test tree goes from 610 files to 510.

docs.title: coxswain-tools
docs.text:
• A chair on a postgres store refuses the chair when its store lease cannot be acquired, where it had fallen back to the lock file; the files store keeps the fallback, and a failed renewal of a held lease still only warns (tools #1794).
  • The chair unit's effective PATH is read across the unit file and its *.conf drop-ins, the last to set PATH winning (tools #1793). The doctor's chair unit PATH row checks that value and names the file it came from, and cox setup migrate rewrites a drop-in that still names the old checkout root with a new chair_unit_dropin step, restarting the chair only when it was running (tools #1796).
  • Fetching a remote run keeps the state of a task whose store row was updated after the run started (tools #1797).
  • cox setup migrate recreates each virtualenv with the optional-dependency groups the old one satisfied, dev always among them, where it had installed .[dev] only and dropped extras such as postgres. A group counts when every distribution it names has a dist-info folder in the old .venv; when the old venv cannot be read it installs .[dev] and prints migrate: <repo> venv extras unknown; installed .[dev] only (tools #1798, tools #1799).
  • The byte-for-byte help snapshot suite, its fixtures and the help-wording tests are removed (tools #1791), and so is the pytest --regen option (tools #1795).
  • The stats CLI tests drop duplicated cases in the examples, ingest and query suites (tools #1792).
  • The suite goes from 7,158 test functions at v0.44.0 to 7,175.

docs.text:
From 0.44.0, still open: some of what docs/design/coxswain-home.md promises is not built. The doctor has no lane host paths or migration state row, and profile paths does not check umbrella_dir. The migration marker records only the old and new roots, not the last finished step. Cut on 2026-10-18. Status: beta. A hardening release from moving the maintainers' own machines under the coxswain home. cox setup migrate --finish can now finish: a lane host that reports a folder inside a moved checkout counts as migrated, and a second --apply after the move keeps the migration marker and plans no drop-in rewrite. The migration also rewrites the profile's repo_map entries for the moved checkouts. The chair's status line counts lanes across every host, an empty queue with idle lanes pushes one notice, and the loop pulls issues at most every ten minutes, where it had exhausted the GitHub GraphQL limit. Only coxswain-tools changes.

cox setup migrate --finish finishes. A lane host's beat lists coxswain-cartridges/providers among its repositories, and the check for a migrated host wanted every path directly under the installs folder, so --finish answered finish: waiting on host <name> to migrate for every host however long it waited. A path anywhere inside the installs folder now counts. After the move every profile setting names the installs folder, so a second cox setup migrate --apply resolved the old root to the installs folder itself: it overwrote migrate.json with the old root equal to the new one, and it planned the chair unit drop-in rewrite on every run, so the local plan never came down to the single skip that --finish waits for. The marker is now written only while the old root differs from the installs folder, and the unit and drop-in steps are planned only when a folder actually moves.

The migration rewrites repo_map. The profile's repo_map, which maps a repository name to its checkout, kept naming the old checkout folders after a migration and had to be rewritten by hand before --finish removed the compatibility links. A repo_map value that equals an old checkout path, in its absolute or tilde spelling, is now rewritten to the checkout under the installs folder in one rewrite_profile_key step, and every other entry is left as it is. A second run plans nothing for it.

The chair sees the whole fleet. The status line's lanes part reads lanes L/C (here l/c) when there are lane hosts: L and C add every host's live lanes and capacity to the chair's own, which stay in the parenthesis. It had shown only the chair's machine, lanes 0/4 while ten lanes were building elsewhere. An empty queue now pushes one notice, Queue empty, when no initiative has a ready task, no intake is queued, no task is approved, no lane is live on any host and the tick raised no hold; it pushes once until the queue fills again. And the issue pull, which the chair planned on every idle tick for every routed repository, now waits ten minutes after the last one.

Cut on 2026-10-18. Status: beta. A hardening release that closes the known gaps 0.43.0 to 0.46.0 left open around the coxswain home and the chair loop. The migration now moves the umbrella and 0.40-style installs, lists operator scripts it cannot rewrite and beats when it ends. The doctor gains the rows the home design promised. The chair holds an approved task's files until it lands and resolves appended test conflicts at land. Several commands now refuse input that used to be accepted and then fail later. Only coxswain-tools changes.

The migration finishes on every layout. cox setup migrate now moves the umbrella checkout (coxswain) under the installs folder with a compatibility link when it is present, so its ../coxswain-tools dependency resolves after --finish. A host without an umbrella plans nothing for it. An install from 0.40.0 that keeps bare-named checkouts behind coxswain-<name> links was refused; the plan now moves the link's target and relinks the old path. A successful --apply lists every operator script that still names an old checkout folder, as migrate: <file> still names <old path>; edit it by hand, and ends with a host beat, so --finish no longer waits for the next beat.

The doctor checks what the migration touches. profile paths now checks umbrella_dir when it is set, and a new lane host paths row fails when a lane host still beats a checkout path outside the installs folder. The home paths row accepts a provider profile kept in the team's workspace, which no migration moves. The forge row asks the GitHub API for the login (gh api user) instead of gh auth status, which rejected a working GH_TOKEN after a rate-limit episode.

The chair keeps parallel work from colliding. An initiative whose tasks are approved but not yet landed now holds its files against new launches, as a running one does; a second initiative had built on the same function four times and conflicted at land each time. When a phase squash conflicts only in test files where both sides append new lines at the end, the land keeps both sides instead of stopping. An empty decompose now holds with the lint refusal from its log instead of refusal line not found.

Commands refuse what they cannot do. cox route file refuses a --repo, or a repo: in the intake's frontmatter, that is not a git checkout on this machine, with route file: refusing, <repo> is not a git checkout on this machine and exit 2; such intakes used to file and then fail every launch. cox host beat <name> refuses a name other than this machine's, since the beat records this machine's facts. cox runs triage takes --profile and --repo, so it reads the profile's store and a named repository from any folder. cox chair watchdog --install writes the five-minute timer the watchdog was meant for (a launchd job on macOS, a systemd user timer on Linux), --uninstall removes it, and --interval-minutes changes the period.

Cut on 2026-10-19. Status: beta. The first monorepo release, and the first with a CalVer number. Coxswain is now one repository, ppfenning/coxswain, and one package, coxswain, with one command, cox. The tools, the harness and graphs, the cartridges and the crew live under src/tools, src/graphs, src/cartridges and crew/, each with its full git history. coxswain-dash (towpath) stays its own repository and an optional --with dash. Nothing new for users beyond the move: 0.47.0's behaviour is carried over, plus the fixes below.

One checkout, one venv. A machine now holds one checkout at ~/.local/share/coxswain/installs/coxswain with one venv, and cox is that checkout installed as a uv tool. Every harness launch, the chair unit's PATH, the store CLI and the doctor take their interpreter from one rule: the checkout's .venv, or on a machine that has not moved yet, the harness checkout's own. A chair on the new layout can still route to a lane host on the old one until that host migrates.

Moving from 0.47. Update cox first: brew upgrade cox, or uv tool uninstall coxswain-tools && uv tool install coxswain. Then cox setup migrate shows the plan and cox setup migrate --apply carries it out: it checks out the release in the umbrella checkout (which becomes the monorepo), syncs its venv, rewrites the profile's harness_dir, skills_roots, umbrella_dir and the default provider_profile, repoints the workspace cartridge links, re-registers the plugin marketplace, swaps the coxswain-tools and agent-cartridges uv tools for coxswain with the same extras, refreshes the chair unit, and moves the old component checkouts to installs/.retired-<date>/. Nothing is deleted. A second run plans nothing. See From 0.47 to the monorepo.

Versions. YYYY.M.N, tagged vYYYY.M.N: the year, the month without a leading zero, and the count of releases cut that month. Every 0.x tag sorts below every CalVer tag, so cox upgrade moves forward from 0.47.0. Compatibility is carried by the store and workspace schema and by cox setup migrate, not by the number.

One release. A release is one version bump, one tag, one PyPI publish of coxswain, one GitHub release and one Homebrew formula PR. The rehearsal takes one commit: a fresh install, and an upgrade from a real 0.47.0 install followed by cox setup migrate.

Cut on 2026-10-19. Status: beta. The first update to the monorepo, built by the lanes in the new repository. It fixes what moving four real machines to 2026.10.0 turned up, runs every test suite in parallel, and trims the largest test files.

The move from 0.47 works on real machines. cox setup migrate copies a team provider profile kept inside the old cartridges checkout into the home and points provider_profile at the copy; writes repo_map back as one-line JSON the profile reader accepts; releases its checkout leases when it ends and says so when a release fails; and fetches the release tag into a shallow checkout and syncs the venv before anything runs the checkout's interpreter. cox install clones the checkout at its own release tag when the home has none, so a first install needs no clone by hand. Syncing the checkout's venv keeps packages installed into it by hand, so plugins survive cox upgrade.

Faster checks. Every test suite runs with pytest-xdist, in CI and in the lanes' checks: the four suites finish in about a minute and a quarter instead of five and a half. The extras job stays serial, because its Postgres store tests back the test database up with pg_dump. Lanes check every component suite through a root .agent-checks file. The largest test files are consolidated to one literal-input test per rule. On pull requests CI no longer runs the Python 3.15 job, which takes about twenty minutes; it runs on every push to main.

Smaller fixes. The five-hour spend estimate counts from the meter's window against the profile's window ceiling, and towpath marks an estimated fraction as one. A decomposed intake's row turns decomposed and links its initiative, so the empty-queue notice fires again. A release commits its releases-index rewrite even when the version needs no bump.

Cut on 2026-10-23. Status: beta. A patch for what running one target repository's work through the chair turned up, plus a docs pass.

Filing and launching one-task work. cox route file without --intake names the task <slug>-task and files the initiative row in the store beside it. Before, the task shared its initiative's id, the store kept only one of the two rows, and launch refused with no initiative row; route edit could not address the task either. --body given text instead of a path says so instead of printing the whole body as a file name.

Logins. A lapsed Claude login stops the run without quarantining the task or spending an attempt, so the next launch on a logged-in host builds it. The remote login check runs the claude binary (command claude), not a shell function of that name: a startup file's claude() wrapper made the check pass while every lane on that host failed to authenticate.

Remote runs come back. cox runs fetch, and so the chair's fetch of an ended remote run, finds the host the way cox route launch --on does: the hosts table first, then the profile's lane_hosts, drained hosts included. It read only the profile, so a run launched on a hosts-table host could never be fetched and its approved tasks never landed.

Cartridges. A cartridge the workspace's cartridges_dir lacks is read from the ones this checkout ships, so a workspace needs only its own team cartridge and never a symlink into one machine's install.

Faster CI. The extras job runs one job per suite, each still serial with its own Postgres, so CI takes about three minutes instead of six.

Docs. A component's pulled README no longer replaces its page, and the pulled component pages and the generated CLI pages join the nav, so every page has previous and next links. The docs call the routing session the chair throughout, and stale claims about bare cox, install, migrate and upgrade are corrected.

Optional extras survive a brew upgrade. The new cox setup extras installs the traces, parquet, lake and postgres extras into the running cox's own environment from pinned, hashed wheels generated from uv.lock, so a Homebrew install no longer needs hand-injected packages. --with picks a subset and --dry-run prints the plan. Cut on 2026-10-31. Status: beta. A release that places lanes across every host and checks their tools before a launch, adds a live view of what each run is doing, lets a bare cox resume or take over the chair, and narrows the GitHub board to open epics. It also makes landing harder to break, and it adds one store migration.

Lanes are placed by the hosts table. cox route launch with no --on picks a host from the hosts table, prints the host and its slots in use, and refuses rather than overfill a host. Before any copy it checks that each tool the repo's checks call is on the chosen host's lane PATH, and it refuses with the missing tool's name. Remote lanes build on the chair's current commit, and a launch whose base cannot be resolved on the chair refuses instead of building on a stale one. cox runs wait, runs move and runs stop now see remote lanes and every host in the table.

A live view of each run. cox runs top shows each run's lease, heartbeat and elapsed time, and a run's nodes expand to show node, turns, last tool and cost. A lane host writes its progress into the store with each heartbeat, so a remote run's progress appears too. A run whose lease another holder took is reported as fenced in runs top, runs detail, status and watch. route launch refuses to relaunch it, and chair clear and cleanup leave live runs alone.

Bare cox resumes, attaches or takes over the chair. With no label, cox takes a free chair, resumes your own, or offers to take over a live holder's chair, open a session that is not the chair, or cancel. A takeover asks the holder to release and waits a short grace. cox route leader status is new and prints one line saying who holds the chair.

The GitHub board tracks open epics. Under tracker_scope: epics, only epics get issues, and a settled epic with no issue is skipped unless tracker_backfill: true is set. Each synced epic carries a checklist of its tasks, ticked when a task is done. cox route sync --prune-out-of-scope closes task issues and removes cards outside the narrowed scope; --dry-run lists them first. Sync also refuses a board that lacks a State option, and it sets a Release field and an epic milestone.

Repos that land on another branch, or by hand. A repo's base: setting, or --base, names the branch it lands on, and runs land, its PRs, runs stranded and the epic harness all use it; phase branches are cut from origin/<base> after a fetch. A repo set to land: manual is skipped by runs land. Once a person merges its PR, the chair marks the task done.

Landing is harder to break. A land runs the team cartridge's checks and then the repo's own, each line in its own shell in the land worktree. It regenerates a generated file that conflicts instead of aborting, and it keeps its leases renewed while it waits on checks. It takes over a repo lease whose holder process is gone. A task whose land conflicts can be sent back for a rebuild, and the next epic run builds it. A test that fails under parallel workers is rerun once on its own before the task is quarantined. cox stats flaky lists tests that needed that rerun three or more times in a week.

Fleet state in a herdr pane, and a fix to the five-hour estimate. cox runs herdr reports fleet state to a herdr pane: blocked when work is approved but not landed, or when a lane's host stops renewing its lease. When the usage meter is stale, the five-hour spend estimate now uses the active ccusage block instead of summing from a reset hours or days old. In coxswain-dash, towpath shows spend inside slipstream, gives every pane one status colour map, colours the queue bar by state, and shows in history whether an approved run's tasks landed.

docs.title: Upgrading
docs.text:
The store schema moves from version 13 to 14: migration 0014 adds a progress column to the leases table. No manual step is needed. The harness applies the migration the first time it opens the store to write, and it saves a backup copy first; a Postgres store needs pg_dump on the PATH for that backup. cox only reads the store and treats the column as empty until then. An older harness refuses to open a store that is at version 14, so upgrade every lane host that shares a store along with the chair. This release declares no cox migrate migrations.

docs.title: Start here
docs.text:
Coxswain is an agent platform in one repository, ppfenning/coxswain, shipped as one package, coxswain, with one command, cox. The repository holds the cox CLI (src/tools), the graphs and the harness that runs them (src/graphs), the cartridges (src/cartridges), the crew seats (crew), and the docs you are reading. The dashboard, towpath, is a separate, optional install.

Coxswain is beta. See What beta means below before you rely on it for anything you can't afford to redo by hand.

docs.title: The loop
docs.text:
Every change a crew makes goes through the same loop. See it as a diagram.

Work arrives as intake: a ticket, a bug report, a request from a human. The coxswain dispatches it, but only within the in-flight bound — a cap on how many runs are active at once, so the crew doesn't take on more than it can review. Once dispatched, a run plans the work, builds it, and is reviewed twice over: once against the team's charter (the style and correctness rules a reviewer holds work to) and once by an adversary looking for what the charter reviewer missed. The two reviews are arbitrated into a single verdict, the result is validated against the checks the project actually runs, and the change lands on a branch. From there it becomes a pull request, and a human — or CI, or both — decides whether it merges on green.

No step in that loop writes to the system of record except the one that owns it. See conventions: single writer for why.

docs.title: What you'll see
docs.text: cox route status shows which provider and model tier a run will use before it starts.

docs.title: Vocabulary
docs.text:
• crew — the agents that do the rowing: they plan, build, review, and validate. The coxswain steers; the crew rows.
  • seat — one role in the crew, filled by one agent doing one job on one run: builder, charter reviewer, adversary, arbiter, validator.
  • coxswain — the component that dispatches work to the crew and enforces the in-flight bound. It never does the crew's work itself.
  • cartridge — a packaged bundle of context for a team or a repo: its conventions, its charter, its thresholds.
  • fragment — one piece of context text — a convention, a charter, a style note — that gets assembled into a seat's prompt for a run.
  • graph — the ordered set of nodes a run executes: plan, build, review, arbitrate, validate, and so on. Defined once, reused by every run.
  • phase — an ordered stage inside an epic. Tickets within a phase aren't necessarily ordered against each other; phases are.
  • task — one unit of work: one ticket, one pull request. If a task needs three PRs, it was really three tasks.
  • run — one execution of a graph against one task, from intake to landing on a branch.
  • docket — the queue of tasks waiting to be dispatched, respecting the in-flight bound.
  • ledger — the record of what a run did: the evidence, the verdicts, the patch. What a human reads to decide whether to trust the result.

docs.title: What beta means
docs.text: Things may change between releases — a flag, a file layout, a command's shape can move without a deprecation cycle. What doesn't move is the version: a release is one tag, vYYYY.M.N, on one repository, and your checkout sits at that tag, so cox versions always tells you exactly what you have. When a release changes the layout on disk or the store's schema, cox setup migrate moves you across.

docs.title: The loop
docs.text:
The same loop described on the Start page, as a diagram. Each node below is one stage a task passes through, in order.

flowchart LR
    intake[Intake] --> dispatch[Dispatch]
    dispatch --> plan[Plan]
    plan --> build[Build]
    build --> charter[Charter review]
    build --> adversary[Adversary review]
    charter --> arbitrate[Arbitrate]
    adversary --> arbitrate
    arbitrate --> validate[Validate]
    validate --> branch[Land on branch]
    branch --> pr[Pull request]
    pr --> merge[Merge on green]

Intake. A ticket, a bug report, or a request enters the docket. Nothing runs yet — intake only records that the work exists and is scoped enough to plan.

Dispatch. The coxswain picks the next task off the docket and starts a run for it, but only if doing so stays within the in-flight bound. The coxswain is the only thing that writes to the docket's state.

Plan. The run breaks the task into an ordered set of steps and names the files it expects to touch, so the reviewers downstream have a boundary to check the work against.

Build. A builder seat does the work in a disposable worktree and produces a patch. It never applies the patch anywhere itself.

Charter review. A reviewer seat holds the patch against the team's charter: its style, its conventions, its correctness rules.

Adversary review. A second reviewer seat looks at the same patch for what the charter review's frame wouldn't catch: edge cases, missing tests, claims without evidence.

Arbitrate. The two verdicts are reconciled into one. Disagreement between them is a finding in itself, not something averaged away.

Validate. The patch is checked against the project's own commands — the ones it actually runs, not a description of them.

Land on branch. Once validated, the patch is applied to a branch. This is the first point in the loop where anything is written outside the disposable worktree.

Pull request. The branch becomes a pull request, carrying the ledger of what happened as evidence for the human who reviews it.

Merge on green. The pull request merges once its checks pass. Nothing upstream of this step is a system of record; this is where the change becomes one.
